entries.en: History of Asaseo Wharf 1
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k197; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
About 700 years ago, Asaseo Wharf was sea.
Strictly speaking, it was a stretch of shallows, and records show that clam digging was popular there.
This was back when villages of just a few houses were scattered here and there.

It must have been a magnificent sight, unimaginable in today's concrete surroundings.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k198; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en: History of Asaseo Wharf 2
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k199; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
By about 500 years ago, about half of the shallows had been reclaimed, and a town like a post town was built.
At this time, people around here still mostly traveled by land.
However, in the remaining shallows, a few shops each monopolized their own area by paying a particular tax, and gathered and sold clams and other catches from there.
Some apparently even charged ordinary people a fee to enjoy clam digging during the holiday season.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k200; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en: History of Asaseo Wharf 3
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k201; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
About 300 years ago at Asaseo Wharf, the shallows were completely reclaimed, and the coast was transformed into a landing dock built of wooden frames.
This can be called the origin of today's wharf.
This dramatically improved distribution by sea routes, and the surrounding towns reportedly prospered.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k202; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en: History of Asaseo Wharf 4
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k203; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
About 150 years ago, the landing docks and storehouses for cargo were expanded, making it one of the three largest landing docks in the country at the time.
As a key point on sea routes, the town reportedly developed even further.

The surrounding farmland, too, turned into houses, shops, and lodgings.
And so it rapidly transformed from a farming town into a commercial town.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k204; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en: History of Asaseo Wharf 5
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k205; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
During the war, when things had become quite modernized, there was also a shipyard, where a few giant battleships were built.
Around it were lodgings and entertainment facilities for the people working at the shipyard, and the money spent by workers gathered from the provinces made the town even more prosperous.

After the war, the shipyard was closed, and where it once stood became new landing docks and a warehouse district, roughly the same as Asaseo Wharf today.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k206; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Warehouse Contents That Vanished Overnight

The long history of Asaseo Wharf contains all sorts of mysterious events.
About 70 years ago, the cargo stored in the wharf's warehouses vanished overnight.
The workers who owned and managed each warehouse had checked the inventory inside their warehouses before going home,
so it's not as if the cargo was never there.

There were security guards patrolling at night back then too, and they say they didn't see anyone carrying anything out.
The cargo in the wharf's warehouses weighed several hundred tons at the very least.
Who on earth carried away so much cargo unnoticed, and how?　
The truth remains unknown to this day.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k218; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Warehouse District with No Exit

Asaseo Wharf is lined with a great many warehouses.
It is said that once you step into the warehouse district, sometimes it goes on and on no matter how far you walk, and you can't get out.
Records also show several cases of workers who headed into the warehouse district and never came back.
Some say they may simply have left the wharf another way and moved elsewhere,
but perhaps they are still wandering the warehouse district even now.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k220; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Children's Laughter Heard at the Wharf Late at Night

It is said that at Asaseo Wharf, from spring to early summer, the excited voices of children can be heard late at night.
Hearing the voices doesn't bring any misfortune, but people find it eerie, so late-night patrols during that season reportedly pay more.

There is information that long ago this area was shallows where clam digging was popular.
Perhaps the happy voices of the children of that time are being heard across the ages.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k222; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Mysterious Employee Mr. Yamazaki

Among the people who work at Asaseo Wharf, there is a well-known employee named Mr. Yamazaki.
This Mr. Yamazaki actually doesn't belong to any company connected with the wharf, and it's doubtful whether he's even human.

That's because, although he appears to be in his early forties, his existence has been confirmed for over 200 years.

Mr. Yamazaki is well versed in all kinds of knowledge, and whenever someone at the wharf is in trouble, he casually shows up and gives precise advice, so the people who work at the wharf reportedly welcome him.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k224; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Calico Cat That Lives On at the Wharf

At Asaseo Wharf there is a calico cat that has lived there since who knows when.
It has a distinctive pattern on its back, and that cat seems to have been hanging around for about 100 years.

It isn't usually seen, but now and then it wanders in, sits with its paws tucked under for a while, and wanders off again.
What matters is that misfortune is said to always strike the companies and people connected with the place where the cat stopped and sat, on the very next day.

The day after it was seen sunbathing atop the steel frame of a gantry crane, that crane collapsed, crashed into a nearby tanker, and went up in a huge blaze.
Another time, it was seen lying in a certain warehouse, and the next day the headquarters of the company that owned the warehouse burned to the ground in a suspicious fire.

The people who work at the wharf believe the cat doesn't bring bad luck, but comes to warn them.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k226; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Corner of the Wharf No One Can Enter

It is said that Asaseo Wharf has an area that can't be reached no matter what.
On the map it seems to be one of the warehouses, but no matter which road you take, you can't get there.

Someone reportedly took aerial footage to check, and in the footage the warehouse could indeed be seen, just as on the map.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k228; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Statue That Patrols at Night

A bronze statue of a certain old man once stood at Asaseo Wharf.
It was a statue of Tokuzo Yano, a local notable, erected in recognition of his generous donations and his efforts to attract business partners when Asaseo Wharf was modernized.

There are people who say they saw Yano's statue patrolling the wharf late at night.
Perhaps the feelings of the man, who loved this wharf throughout his life, still remained in the statue.

The statue is now kept at the city museum. Honoring his achievements, the city intends to keep the statue in good condition and aims to have it designated a national treasure.
So far, there seem to be no sightings of the statue patrolling the museum.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k230; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
One thing you often see at wharves is a big thing shaped like a giraffe.
This is called a "gantry crane."

The people who work at the wharf use these gantry cranes to load containers onto ships and, the other way around, lift up containers loaded on ships.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k232; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Asaseo Wharf has lots of warehouses.
They store cargo brought by big ships, and cargo to load the next time a ship comes.

There are many kinds of warehouses, too: some keep things cold like the fridge at your house, and some keep them frozen rock-solid like a freezer.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k234; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The boxes of different colors piled up all over Asaseo Wharf are called "containers."

People put all kinds of cargo inside these containers and carry them on big ships.
It's just like when you put your toys in a box to carry them.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k236; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Where ships stop at the wharf, there are lots of things lined up that look like a thick, bent index finger. These are called "bitts."
By tying these bitts to the ship with a thiiick rope, the ship is kept from moving on its own.

Their size and shape can differ depending on the wharf or port, so check them out when you go there with your mom and dad.
But be very careful not to fall into the sea.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k238; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
When you look at the sea from the wharf, you can see triangular things bobbing on the water.
These are called "lighted buoys," and they are markers so ships don't get lost.

They light up at night, but there are no outlets nearby.
So how do they make electricity? By bobbing back and forth on the waves.

Small models are on sale too, so buy one and try it out.

entries.en: Before dawn today, the flower of the giant plant that had taken hold of the Akashia Department Store at the Umegaya intersection burst. The surrounding area was engulfed in a dazzling flash, and the city was reportedly completely destroyed.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0095.json:p0/k70; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Umegaya Park, devastated by the giant plant's burst.
Online, people are lamenting the park's disappearance. The park was proposed in 1966 by the mayor at the time, so that citizens wouldn't lose a place of peace amid the city's development. The city council at the time unanimously approved it.
Long beloved as a place for citizens to relax, its disappearance has shocked nearby residents.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0095.json:p0/k82; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Information has come in that Yuko Saeki, wanted on suspicion of murdering her brother, may have fled into the area around Azami 1-chome Station, where an evacuation order had been issued.
The area has been reduced to ruins by the giant plant's burst, and Saeki's safety is unknown.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0095.json:p0/k90; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Before dawn today, our reporter captured riot police vehicles and civilians, who began evacuating just before the flower of the giant plant on the Akashia Department Store at the Umegaya intersection exploded, fleeing at full speed from the oncoming blast.
The two civilians were on a motorcycle, and the reporter says it took everything he had just to keep up on foot.

entries.en:
Our news helicopter captured a Metropolitan Police Labor descending to the ground holding a girl.
This Labor is the "AV-98 Ingram" of the 2nd Platoon, Special Vehicles Section 2, MPD Security Division. It was reportedly deployed for this rescue because it is more mobile and capable of more precise movements than the Fire Department's Labor, the "CRL-98 Pyrobuster."
Judging by this girl's smile, this sortie can be called a great success.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k168; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"A fire Labor saved me!" When we interviewed people caught up in the building fire, we heard this over and over.
Mr. Sakurada of Kunshiran Construction, who says he is alive thanks to a fire Labor, was heading for the emergency exit when the ceiling suddenly collapsed and the flames blocked his way.
Just when he thought, "This is it...," a fire Labor appeared from the atrium at the center of the Iberis Tower Building and began spraying water, and after the fire was out, it watched over him until he had safely passed through.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k172; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The wreckage of a Labor of unknown affiliation, the "TYPE-5Q/2C Graubear," was found in the ruins of the Iberis Tower Building fire.
The pilot has not been found, and judging from the damage, it appears to have fallen down the atrium at the center of the building.
No information could be obtained from people connected to the tower, and it is believed to have entered from outside. Its connection to the fire is unknown.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k174; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"A blue Labor was blowing up the building." Mr. Terayama, who was doing air-conditioning work at the Iberis Tower Building, says he heard the fire alarm and was evacuating when a wall suddenly collapsed and a blue Labor appeared.
The blue Labor rampaged across the floor and then headed for the floor below.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k176; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Around 9:00 p.m. today, Mr. Komori, who was viewing the night scenery on the observation floor of the Iberis Tower Building, noticed the sound of a helicopter.
Looking around, he says he saw a blue Labor being carried to the roof. Could it be connected to the building fire?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k178; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Around 9:30 p.m. today, Kunshiran Construction's headquarters was attacked by a blue Labor and its safe was stolen.
According to an announcement by Kunshiran Construction's PR section, the attack resulted in the theft of the safe and the loss of important documents, but there was no external impact such as leaks of personal or corporate information.
The blue Labor's affiliation is unknown, but Kunshiran Construction had long faced fierce protests from the environmental group NKX that could be taken as a declaration of intent, and the Miyato Prefectural Police, believing the group is involved, indicated it will seek to question the group's leader, Kiyoharu Futamura.

entries.en: "I'll Keep Letting Them Go By": Muto
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k211; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The MiyaSpo! Start Dash Award, honoring the most impressive fielder in the first week of the season, has been announced, going to Kunshiran Elephants third baseman Muto (27).
In the 9th inning of the April 2 game against the Giraffes, Muto let a grounder go by that would have been a walk-off if fair, and it rolled foul; he then hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the 10th inning of extras to lead the team to victory.
The next day he went 4-for-4 with 6 RBIs, powering the Elephants to first place.
In the postgame interview, when he learned he'd won the award, he said, "It's my first time, so I'm really happy. I'll keep letting the tough grounders go by," getting laughs by poking fun at his shaky defense.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k212; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
We of the Hearty Appetite Squad heard rumors that the sandwiches sold at Café Iberis on the observation floor of the Iberis Tower Building are hugely popular and sell out quickly every day, so we went to investigate!

The No. 1 most popular is the "Iberis Tower Sandwich"! Sandwiched between bread as soft and chewy as marshmallow is... a deep-fried mochi!?
This mochi, eaten with tartar sauce made from fresh-picked vegetables and rich eggs, is no ordinary mochi!
This mochi (is it even mochi...?), kneaded with sticky rice, corn, red beans, and pumpkin, has gooey white sauce inside!
They say it's then breaded and deep-fried. Its carb content per serving is an astonishing three rice balls' worth! (122 grams!)
We lined up right after opening to buy one and took a bite at once, and it's delicious!
If you want one, you might find them sold out unless you arrive before opening. Café Iberis opens at 11:00, by the way.
The superb "Ham and Egg Sandwich" and "Wagyu Steak Sandwich" are also out of this world, so give them a try.

entries.en: Pippi the Hamster Rescued
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k244; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Pippi the hamster, kept in an office of the Iberis Tower Building, survived the fire.
Pippi was kept in a cage at the back of the bottom drawer of a certain desk in an office in the southeast corner of the tower's 19th floor, and although the fire had spread to that room, there were signs that a fire extinguisher had been used, so someone apparently happened to put out the fire around the desk where Pippi was.
T, who kept Pippi, said, "I want to thank them somehow. I'm truly, truly grateful to whoever saved Pippi, whom I abandoned."

entries.en: Late-Night Snack Thief Appears
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k246; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Do you know the term "fire-scene thief"? It refers to someone who steals amid the chaos of a fire or similar situation, and there was just such an incident in the Iberis Tower Building fire.
S, who works on the 19th floor of the Iberis Tower Building, couldn't possibly finish work that day and, resigned to working late into the night, bought a Cherry Blossoms in Full Bloom bento at the nearby convenience store Clover.
Then the fire broke out, and S left the bento behind and evacuated. When S returned to the office after the fire was out, the bento that had been on the desk was nowhere to be found.
S says, "If they were desperately hungry in the middle of a fire, I can't blame them, but I wish they'd at least left the money."

entries.en: The Solo Boom!
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k250; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
As more and more young people say they have "never dated" or "have no desire to marry," the Iberis Tower Building, famous for its night view, was bustling with couples again today.
Movie theaters, amusement parks, and night-view spots are classic date spots, but many people feel they are "hard to go to alone."
Asked why, many give extreme persecution fantasies like "If I'm alone, couples will think I'm a 'lonely loser,'" but this writer understands all too well how it feels to be made to feel small. Yet since the start of this year, more and more active people are going all sorts of places alone, says solo expert Ms. T (24 years of going solo), who does not just karaoke and yakiniku but even movie theaters and amusement parks.
"If you worry about the people around you, you can't do anything you like. Overthinking it is bad. You should enjoy your own life on your own terms."
Ms. T has a point. Maybe going solo isn't something to worry about after all?

entries.en: The Perfect Place to Propose?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k252; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Spring is the season of love. Perhaps many of you are thinking of proposing to your partner?
In our survey last month, the No. 1 most popular place to propose in Miyato Prefecture was the Iberis Tower Building!
Here are the reasons people voted for it!

"I want to be proposed to while looking at a beautiful night view" (Ms. A, office worker)
"It feels so out of the ordinary, I'd say yes on the spot" (Ms. M, teacher)
"Dinner is expensive, so I wouldn't be embarrassed to tell anyone" (Ms. P, helping out at home)
"The restrooms are clean" (Mr. I, food service)

Did that help?
Men planning to take the plunge this spring, take note.

entries.en: Suspicious Man in a Lab Coat at the Fire Scene
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k256; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
There have been a string of eyewitness reports of a man in a lab coat at the fire scene.
The man in the lab coat was wandering the 20th floor, unfazed by the fire, muttering something.
There was no man in a lab coat among those rescued, and police are investigating the remains of the fire.

entries.en: The Scent of Roasted Sweet Potatoes?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k258; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Iberis Tower Building is said to smell wonderful.
At the time of the fire, the sweets café Ibe Gelato on the 2nd floor of the Iberis Tower Building was preparing a new product, the Sweet Potato Sandwich, to launch tomorrow.
They were steaming a huge amount of sweet potatoes when the fire alarm went off. A clerk mistakenly evacuated with the heat still on, but instead of burning to a crisp, the potatoes came out perfectly roasted, and the street outside is filled with a delicious roasted sweet potato aroma.
Not knowing what to do with all the roasted sweet potatoes, Ibe Gelato is reportedly handing them out to the onlookers gathered at the fire.
Ibe Gelato was unaffected by the fire and will reopen as soon as it can. We can't wait for that sweet potato sandwich.

entries.en: Volunteers Stopped
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k260; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
A volunteer effort has been stopped. Around 9:30 p.m. today, in response to the Iberis Tower Building fire in Sakura Ward, Miyato City, Miyato Prefecture, Soji Kawaji, who runs the nearby public bath Shime no Yu, proposed fighting the fire using the bathhouse's hot water.
Mr. T, owner of the home center across from Shime no Yu, also cooperated and donated a large number of buckets, and about 30 young people from the neighborhood started a bucket relay to pass along the hot water.
The relay followed a rule where 20 people each carried the water about 15 m to the building entrance, and the remaining 10 waited at the entrance, each heading off to fight the fire once they received a bucket, but 10 minutes after it began, the Fire Department arrived, warned them it was dangerous, and the volunteer effort was called off.
K, a Miyato University student who led the line, said:
"Thinking our actions might save someone, I joined in without even thinking. I took the inside of the building without much thought, but the fire was above the 14th floor, so the distance just the 10 of us at the front had to cover was endless. The buckets were very heavy, but I figured people's lives are heavier, and since I'd taken it on, I wanted to do my best."
With Mr. T's permission, everyone reportedly took their buckets home.

entries.en: Idol Fans Unfazed by Fire
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k262; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Starting at 8:00 p.m. today, a handshake event for the underground idol unit "Mo-Mo-Mo Dynamite" (Momomo) was held in the event hall on the 12th floor of the Iberis Tower Building.
Momomo is popular for its exciting live shows with sparks and explosions, and you'd think a handshake event would be tame... but then the building caught fire!
Staff guided evacuations, but the fans refused, saying things like "It's part of the show, we don't get scared just because the building shakes," making evacuation difficult.
Even Momomo was apparently startled by the fire alarm, though, and when the members themselves guided the evacuation, the fans obediently followed.
Reversible Records, Momomo's label, has announced that it has nothing whatsoever to do with this fire.

entries.en: The Blues of a Young Man Whose Housework Is Seriously Bad
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k266; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
There's a saying listing the four scariest things: earthquakes, thunder, fire, and fathers. But a young man rescued from the Iberis Tower Building fire begs to differ.
"Blackouts are worse than thunder. Fire's bad, but the housework at my place is even worse. My whole life is bad. Fire and thunder don't matter if they don't hit you. Earthquakes and fathers are always scary."
We asked afterward if we could cover his home, but were turned down. Too bad.

entries.en: Binoculars at Night
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k268; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Binoculars at night may let you see far away, but it's dark all around, so they aren't very practical.
The other day, however, there was an incident where nighttime binoculars played a starring role.
Around 10:00 p.m. on the 24th of last month, during a robbery at a Clover convenience store in Sakura Ward, Miyato City, Miyato Prefecture, someone who happened to witness it through the binoculars at the Iberis Tower Building called it in, and the Miyato Prefectural Police rushed to the scene and the incident was resolved without harm.
That day, Ms. N-kawa (a 28-year-old woman) had broken up with the partner she'd dated for five years and, feeling reckless, went up to the observation floor of the Iberis Tower Building.
"I was looking through the binoculars thinking I'm worth about as much as binoculars at night, when I saw someone in a helmet holding a knife go into the convenience store. I called it in without thinking. And to think that got the case solved right away... Maybe I'm still worth something."
The heroic Ms. N-kawa is reportedly now looking for a partner.

entries.en: The Iberis Tower Diet?!
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k270; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Iberis Tower Diet is all the rage.
On the south side of the Iberis Tower Building in Sakura Ward, Miyato City, opposite the entrance, there are staircases at the east and west corners, allowing you to walk back and forth between the 1st and 2nd floors without stopping.
The one who noticed this and named it the Amane Road is super diet advisor Mr. Amaneden.
Mr. Amaneden says, "Walking is truly good for your health, but outside there are cars and traffic lights. Yet treadmills get boring. But on the Amane Road, the scenery changes and you don't have to stop. Just when you get bored, there's a staircase. Even if you get tired, getting home isn't a problem. There's a clock, too. And right now there are diet buddies, so you can keep it up."
Indeed, the south side has little foot traffic, so it seems you can exercise without bothering anyone.
When we went to see for ourselves, people were marching like an army, or rather like a factory.
If you're interested, why not visit the Iberis Tower Building?!

This observation floor is glass on all 360 degrees, letting you look down on the night view of Sakura Ward from every angle.
High-performance binoculars are installed facing every direction, so you can gaze at distant sights and never get bored.
The floor's interior is refined, too, and you and your date are sure to be captivated by this gently glittering space.
Be sure to pay a visit on your next day off.

entries.en: A Father in Despair: "I Never Imagined This Would Happen"
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k274; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Many of the people rescued from the Iberis Tower Building fire were visitors. Norio Nakagawa (55) is one of them.
Norio's daughter, Sakurako Nakagawa, and her partner had told him they wanted to formally ask for his blessing to marry, and he was waiting for them at the Iberis Café on the top floor of the Iberis Tower Building.
When the two didn't show up, Norio tried to contact them but couldn't get through, and just then he happened to learn on his smartphone that the Sky Garden Bridge, which Sakurako and her partner were supposed to cross, had collapsed.
"I opposed the marriage once. I lost my wife when Sakurako was still little... I'd actually planned to give them my blessing today... I never imagined this would happen..."
So far, Sakurako's name is not among the survivors of the Sky Garden Bridge collapse.

entries.en: Charge-In Q-chan: The Suspicious Man Edition
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0125.json:p0/k276; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
So, this week, Q-chan went looking for something worth writing about, and headed to the observation floor of the Iberis Tower Building.
Crowded with young people on their way home from work and couples on dates, it seemed like the perfect place to hear some interesting stories!
Or so I thought as I happily showed up, but after that the tower caught fire... and the whole staff ran for it. But before that, I made sure to talk to someone interesting!
Behind the stairs on the observation floor, I spotted a man crouching and sneakily talking on the phone! He was suspicious to the max, but so suspicious that no one went near him. So, we'll interview him ourselves.

Reporter Q: "Um... sorry to bother you."
Man: "Wh... what is it? Sorry, I'm on the phone right now..."
Reporter Q: "I'm Q, and I post articles on a news site."
Man: "No, I'm on the phone. Give me a break."
Reporter Q: "Sneakily talking on the phone behind the stairs seemed suspi... I mean, interesting. Please, tell me more."
Man: "Hey, this is way too pushy. Who the hell are you?"
Reporter Q: "Is it a work call?"
Man: "That's right. We have an important operation coming up."
Reporter Q: "I see, so it's confidential."
Man: "Huh? Oh, yes, that's right, it's confidential. Sorry, but please go somewhere else."
Reporter Q: "Oh, I see. Excuse me. By the way, I think 'a man who keeps talking on the phone behind the stairs' is interesting. Can I write an article about it?"
Man: "A-An article?!"
Reporter Q: "Yes. I didn't hear anything about your work in the first place, and I'll keep it all under wraps. Let me take a quick photo! Say cheese!"

...And so, the man stayed suspicious to the MAX right to the end, and I couldn't get any details, but it sure is suggestive. I smell something shady. I'm curious. See you tomorrow! (Written by weekly blog Charge-In Q-chan)

entries.en:
On the 3rd of this month, the Miyato Prefecture Nutrition Education Seminar for Working Adults was held in the Iberis Tower Building.
Last month, the Miyato Prefecture Health and Welfare Center led a survey of 250 people working in the Iberis Tower Building about what they eat for lunch,
and found that about 82%, or 204 people, ate lunch at restaurants in the Iberis Tower Building three or more times a week.
"The advantage of eating lunch out is that you can easily get warm, tasty food, but eating out a lot can increase your fat intake and unbalance your nutrition," says Ms. Nashimura, a dietitian at the Health and Welfare Center.
Ms. Nashimura introduced nutrients that tend to be lacking in each type of restaurant food, recommended ingredients to make up for them, and points to watch out for when eating out.
"I hope that by understanding nutrients properly, everyone can enjoy eating out and stay healthy."

entries.en:
Around 3:00 a.m. today, a black giant creature appeared again in Yotsuba Ward, Miyato Prefecture.
It is thought to be the same creature that appeared at Hinageshidai Station.

The giant creature is currently moving toward the Fortune Center Building, causing severe damage to buildings and houses in its path.
Police are desperately calling for evacuation and guiding people, but given the late hour, ensuring residents' safety is extremely difficult, and the damage is gradually spreading.

The Miyato Prefectural Police are urging, "If you are near Yotsuba Ward, follow police instructions, or even without police guidance, leave the area as quickly as possible."

entries.en:
We have just received eyewitness reports that a huge weapon was being transported near a Self-Defense Forces base.

According to the witness, an aircraft that appeared to be a transport plane was carrying something that looked like a huge weapon suspended beneath it.
"It was dark and I could only see a silhouette, but that big silhouette looked just like the black giant creature that appeared at Hinageshidai Station," the witness said.

The transport plane appeared to head toward Yotsuba Ward, and it is speculated that some kind of weapon has been deployed.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0134.json:p0/k156; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The giant creature that had been heading toward the Fortune Center Building suddenly stopped and began destroying the surrounding buildings with beams.

As was also seen at Hinageshidai Station, this giant creature appears able to fire a bluish-white beam from its mouth to destroy buildings and other structures.
This attack has caused devastating damage around the Fortune Center Building, including the total collapse of buildings and fires.
The shock of its occasional roars is also tremendous; the glass of surrounding buildings was seen shattering all at once.

Why the giant creature suddenly began its destruction is unknown, and an expert on creature ecology commented, "At this stage it's hard to predict, and the best thing we can do is get away from the giant creature as soon as possible."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0134.json:p0/k158; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"They told me 'disasters caused by giant creatures are not natural disasters,' and didn't pay out the insurance."
So says Mr. Kawade, owner of the Kawaide Sky Building, shoulders slumped.
Despite his building being completely destroyed by the appearance of the giant creature, he reportedly received no insurance money at all.

In response to such feedback, Oriental Insurance has launched Disaster MAX Insurance, which covers every disaster except man-made ones.
Of course, it fully covers disasters caused by giant creatures like this one! We'll protect your property from every kind of disaster!

Start by getting a quote on Oriental Insurance's information page!

entries.en:
The government has still made no announcement regarding the huge weapon deployed in the urban area around the Fortune Center Building.
The late hour is thought to be one reason for the delay.

A short while ago, Assistant to the Defense Minister Oshiba responded to questions from reporters, but only said, "We are currently confirming the situation. We will make an official announcement later, so please wait a little longer."
Reporters fired off question after question, but the interview was apparently cut off there.

entries.en:
Even though a giant creature appeared, dissatisfaction is rising sharply among nearby residents over the deployment of a weapon in an urban area and its subsequent rampage.
Calls for protest demonstrations are spreading, centered on residents who suffered actual damage, and there were apparently some clashes between residents and police officers, further raising residents' discontent.
Mr. Kawade, the central figure calling for the protests, said, "There's no way using a weapon in the middle of an urban area like this can be allowed. We will protest firmly and demand compensation for this disaster and measures to prevent it from happening again."

entries.en:
Research data has been released showing an increase in recent years in young people who cannot solve problems by thinking for themselves.
According to critic Mr. Sahara, an expert on young people's circumstances, the act of "asking when you don't know something" seems to have turned, before anyone noticed, into "asking even about things you could figure out by thinking."

Mr. Sahara said, "Teaching them everything isn't the answer. Sure, it may be easy for the one asking, but it's pretty hard on the one teaching, too. And there's such a thing as the attitude of the one learning. It might be an old-fashioned way of thinking, but in the old days we were told to 'watch and steal it,' and we desperately watched and tried to learn. I wonder if young people today just don't get that."

Changes in the environment surrounding young people may have created the current situation.

entries.en:
According to the results of a survey of young people in their teens and twenties conducted at the end of last month, young people's positivity this year has risen 16% compared to last year.

The economic recovery and overall improvements in academic ability are considered the main reasons.
This has reportedly given them more emotional room, and in recent years the number of young people with a strong sense of justice has been on the rise.

In response to the results, Mr. Wakabayashi, chair of the NPO "Society for Thinking About Young People," cheered them on: "I think it's a very good trend. It seems our activities so far have paid off. I hope they keep using their youthful energy to build better relationships."

entries.en:
The other day, survey results were released showing an increase in young people who quickly start whining.
It seems there are quite a few cases where they give up over simple things, saying "It's hopeless," losing their drive to improve and damaging their relationships with those around them.

On this issue, critic Mr. Sahara, an expert on young people's circumstances, said, "Because the people around them give up easily, they think 'then I will too,' and give up sooner. Parents in particular should avoid whining in front of their children as much as possible. And the young people themselves can't help what they feel inside, but they'd better refrain from saying it out loud."

Their own behavior matters, of course, but perhaps the environment around young people can also help prevent this.

The rampage of the huge weapon has completely destroyed the Fortune Center Building, known as an office building.
Companies such as Otani Solutions and W&P Consulting had offices in the Fortune Center Building, and their business is expected to be greatly affected.

Several companies have missing employees, and it seems they won't be able to resume business right away tomorrow.
Since there is no precedent for a disaster of this kind, how companies will be compensated will be the key to resuming business.

"I didn't know what was going on. Before I knew it, I was just running and running. It feels strange to be alive like this now."
So said Mr. Tabata, an employee of W&P Consulting.
Tabata is an employee of W&P Consulting, which had its office in the now-destroyed Fortune Center Building.
He was working late into the night that day when he got caught up in this situation.

"I never imagined the whole office would just disappear. What am I supposed to do starting tomorrow?"
he said, voicing his confusion and anxiety.

There are many cases of people losing their homes or workplaces overnight to giant shadows, and finding the cause of the frequent giant shadow appearances is urgent.

Persuaded by firefighters who arrived later, Tabata apparently gave up searching the rubble.

Tabata is a new employee who graduated from university and joined the workforce just last month.
Caught up in this disaster just as he started working life, he seems to have no idea at all what the future holds for his work.
On top of that, another misfortune had befallen Tabata.
Of all things, he had left his pay envelope at the office, and he had been searching for it until just now.
If his pay isn't found, his life will apparently become quite difficult.

It seems Tabata has found himself at a crossroads in life barely after becoming a working adult.

On the way back to the company dorm, he stopped into an izakaya and enjoyed some delicious local fish!

entries.en:
Staff at the Cosmic Ray Research Institute reportedly play shogi during breaks and at other times.
From Deputy Director Sasaki, a devotee of the Static Rook Anaguma, to Chief Researcher Sawada, a devotee of the Fourth-File Rook, each studies their strategies diligently, and the annual "Cosmic Ray Research Institute Cup Shogi Tournament" was a big hit among the staff.

Chief Researcher Sawada said, "It's a real shame that with Deputy Director Sasaki gone, there's no one left at the institute who plays the Static Rook Anaguma. So that we never forget the deputy director's spirit, I want to keep actively promoting shogi at the institute."

Following the theft of orange juice, thought to have been caused by the lack of vending machines at the institute, it has emerged that it also lacks running water and heating to keep researchers healthy.
When this writer investigated, there was no running water for drinking water inside the institute, only a large ventilation system installed in the ceiling
.
Researcher Mr. Hayami of the institute stressed, "Not having any warm-up spots is a matter of life and death."

entries.en:
Late tonight, four giant aliens appeared on a street in Hananira-cho, Miyato City. After brawling for a while, they disappeared. The brawl caused eight nearby buildings to collapse. According to police, 12 residents caught up in the incident were seriously or lightly injured and 1 is missing, and the numbers are expected to rise.
The giant aliens first appeared as three and brawled around Hananira-cho, then resumed fighting as four with the addition of another that appeared. A fierce battle with heat rays flying back and forth took place, causing heavy damage to the surrounding buildings.
One of the giant aliens is believed to be the same silver giant alien that appeared in Sakura Ward yesterday evening.

entries.en:
Late tonight, the brawl between giant aliens in Hananira-cho caused major cave-ins on the surrounding roads. On some roads, the cave-ins are more than 8 m deep, and they are currently closed to traffic.
In addition to the cave-ins, the roads around the scene are completely blocked by rubble from buildings destroyed in the giant aliens' brawl and by damaged cars, so not even work vehicles can get through, and there is currently no prospect of restoration.

entries.en:
A fire broke out in the Ebine Publishing building in Hananira-cho, Miyato City. It appears to have been extinguished. No one was injured in the fire.
The fire is believed to have started in the 2nd Editorial Department on the 6th floor of Ebine Publishing. A fierce battle by giant aliens was taking place nearby, and it is thought to have been caught in the aftermath, but according to firefighters who rushed to the scene, there is also the view that "it may have been caused by a carelessly discarded cigarette," and the cause will be clarified by further investigation.
Ebine Publishing is the publisher of the popular information magazine "Giant Shadow Weekly."

entries.en:
A strange-smell scare was reported at "Convenience Store Clover Hananira-cho West Branch" in Hananira-cho, Miyato City. According to a clerk, a foul smell like a sewer filled the store. The clerk also said, "Now that I think about it, the smell may have started around when a group of three came in, one carrying a woman on their back. It was chaotic, so I don't remember well."
Clover Hananira-cho West Branch has closed for the day for cleaning.
A battle between giant aliens was taking place nearby at the time, and it is thought to be related.

One of the victims, Mr. A (a man in his 30s), said, "My brand-new car, delivered just last week, got blown away. I still have 36 loan payments left, and I'm worried whether my car insurance will cover it."

entries.en: A woman was found in the collapsed rubble inside the sewers of Hananira-cho, Miyato City. The woman reportedly glared at the firefighters who came to rescue her and said, "I wasn't in the rubble because of an accident. I buried myself in the rubble." She disappeared right after being rescued, and a man who saw her at a temporary shelter said, "The look in her eyes wasn't normal. It was creepy. I glanced away for a moment, and she was already gone."

entries.en: While removing debris from the caved-in ground in Hananira-cho, Miyato City, workers found a pot full of koban gold coins. Based on their features, the coins are estimated to be from the early modern period. The pot contained 108 koban, and according to Mr. Yasuda, who runs an old coin shop in Mizuna City, "They're worth at least several million yen. Considering their historical value, they're worth even more."

entries.en: While removing debris from the caved-in ground in Hananira-cho, Miyato City, a skeletonized bone believed to be a human femur was found. The bone appears to have been buried underground for a long time, and police are conducting a detailed analysis. The bone was found beneath a paved main road, and police say, "We are considering the possibility that it was buried during road construction or mixed into the construction soil."

entries.en:
Deep in the caved-in ground in Hananira-cho, Miyato City, a fossil believed to be from the Cretaceous dinosaur Parasaurolophus was found.
The fossil found was of a head, and because of its characteristic crest, it is estimated to be a relative of Parasaurolophus.
On hearing the news, Mr. Onda, chair of the Hananira-cho Chamber of Commerce, said, "We've had enough of giant creatures, but dinosaurs are more than welcome. From now on we want to promote ourselves as 'Hananira, the Dinosaur Town.'"
【Parasaurolophus】
An herbivorous dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous of the Mesozoic (82 to 66 million years ago), 8 to 10 m long and weighing 4 to 6 t. Characterized by a long crest extending from its nose to the back of its head.

entries.en:

This happened when the blue giant alien was cornered by the black alien's attacks; the silver giant alien was seen patting the shoulder of the damaged blue giant alien, down on one knee, as if to encourage it.
Ms. K (a 26-year-old woman), who saw this while fleeing from around the two giants' feet, said, "It really looked like it was encouraging it. Thinking about it that way, the silver giant alien seemed to have a really dignified air."

entries.en:

In the images, the heat rays can be seen fired from three giant aliens, each in a different color and size.
Associate Professor N of S University, an expert in astrophysics, said, "There are creatures on Earth with parts of their bodies that glow, but it's astonishing that they can produce light energy powerful enough to serve as an attack. There's no doubt they are beings completely different from us Earth creatures."

entries.en:
Risa Katsuragi, famous as an avant-garde calligrapher, has been rescued from a building elevator in which she was trapped, her agency announced.
Katsuragi had come to an event hall in Hananira-cho, Miyato City, for an exhibition of her calligraphy when four giant aliens appeared. She got into an elevator to evacuate, but the shock of the giant aliens' roars cut the elevator's power, trapping her.
Katsuragi was rescued an hour later with no serious injuries, but she is exhausted and is currently receiving treatment at a hospital. The event organizer has announced that the exhibition will be postponed until Katsuragi recovers.

entries.en: Grandma Saves the Day: Risako Kusunoki of Mizuna City
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0154.json:p0/k195; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Risako Kusunoki (77) of Mizuna City has made headlines for persuading a man who had been repeatedly stealing amid the chaos of the giant alien incidents to turn himself in at a police box.
Walking home late at night from a nearby convenience store, Kusunoki saw a man trying to break in through a first-floor window of an apartment building. After a staredown, she drew out the troubles that had led him to steal and gave him life advice. The man was persuaded, went with her to a nearby police box, and was arrested.
Kusunoki said, "I was scared, but I thought of my son who lives far away and couldn't just leave him. I hope he turns over a new leaf."

entries.en:
The "Milky Way Film Festival," counted among the world's 100 film festivals, was held in Country F, and the Best Actress award went to Risa Kashiwagi.
The film "Stray Cat Wi-Fi Wasteland," starring Risa Kashiwagi, also won Best Screenplay, and director William Tsuruta said, "I'm deeply honored to leave our name in film history like this. This film could not have been completed without Risa. I'm grateful."
In an interview after winning, Risa Kashiwagi mentioned the giant creature incidents occurring in Miyato City, saying, "I'd like to donate the prize money. I hope for a swift recovery."
(The image is a scene from "Stray Cat Wi-Fi Wasteland.")

entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0154.json:p0/k199; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Vehicles abandoned on the streets around Hananira-cho, Miyato City, have caught fire because of the giant aliens that appeared there.
As the giant aliens fought on the streets, crushed vehicles ignited and exploded, and the fire spread to nearby vehicles, becoming a major blaze.
In addition, the black giant alien kicked up a large truck, which crashed into a tanker truck where it landed, igniting the gasoline aboard and causing a huge explosion. Flames are still rising over a wide area of the Hananira-cho West intersection.

entries.en: Following news of the destruction of Miyato City by giant creatures since yesterday evening, domestic stocks have fallen across the board. Some stocks, such as those related to medicine, construction, and defense, have risen in anticipation of large-scale rescue and reconstruction efforts.

entries.en:
In response to the series of giant alien incidents, an emergency meeting was held at the Prime Minister's Office. The meeting reportedly discussed how to approach negotiations with the giant aliens.
At a press conference, the Chief Cabinet Secretary said, "The giant creatures appear and vanish unpredictably. They currently appear only around Miyato City, but there is a risk the damage will spread to other regions. There are limits to repelling them with our nation's means of defense. The meeting agreed that we should minimize the damage through talks with the aliens."

entries.en:
Amid the giant creature incidents in Miyato City, inquiries about the safety of family members living in the city have flooded a special government website, making it extremely difficult to access.
Masako Umeda, whose son works at a convenience store in Hananira-cho, Miyato City, said, "I can't reach my son, so I'm worried. I just want him to be safe."

entries.en: A new boom seems to be brewing in the coffee industry: "local specialty coffee." Coffee's flavor changes with how the beans are roasted, ground, and brewed, and products modeled on the methods of long-established and popular coffee shops in each region are starting to appear. Kenzo Aiuchi, chair of the Miyato City Coffee Club, said, "I'm glad people can easily enjoy carefully crafted coffee. I hope this becomes a gateway for people to visit the actual shops. My personal dream is that eventually, with more coffee fans, more and more coffee shops will open and the whole city will overflow with the aroma of coffee."

Karaage Minister is a popular Clover product known for its series in a wide variety of flavors.
The company's official PR social media account posted, "Thanks to the support of so many customers, we've achieved the wonderful result of 100 billion units. Next, we're aiming for 1 trillion!"

Giant aliens had appeared nearby around the time the man in the swimsuit was sighted, and a Miyato City Police officer said, "Perhaps he took advantage of the chaos to fulfill a longtime desire to walk around town in a swimsuit."

It has come to light that a woman in a swimsuit entered a convenience store in Hananira-cho, Miyato City. By the time Miyato City Police officers responding to a call arrived, the woman had vanished.
Giant aliens had appeared nearby around the time the woman in the swimsuit was sighted, and a Miyato City Police officer said, "Perhaps she took advantage of the chaos to fulfill a longtime desire to walk around town in a swimsuit."
Unless the swimsuit is extremely sexy, it reportedly isn't a crime.

entries.en:
In response to the series of giant creature appearances in Miyato City, events and concerts scheduled across the country are being canceled one after another.
The popular idol group "Homeostasis," in the middle of a nationwide tour, had a concert scheduled at Aosagi Stadium tomorrow, but announced on its official website, "We are postponing it out of consideration for the audience's safety."
Group leader Shota Hino posted on social media, "About canceling tomorrow's concert: we talked it over with a lot of people and made the decision we thought was best. We're sorry to all the fans who were looking forward to it, but please put your safety first right now."

entries.en: Anime "Sugochikku Mirorin" Episode 27 Postponed Following Giant Creature Incidents
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0154.json:p0/k219; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The broadcaster has announced that Episode 27 of the popular anime "Sugochikku Mirorin" has been postponed due to the appearance of giant aliens.
Episode 27 contains a scene in which a giant-sized Mirorin tries to make ice cream with a concrete mixer truck, and broadcast was postponed because it could remind viewers of the giant creature incidents in Miyato City. Next week's slot will air a substitute program, and the week after will air Episode 28. Whether Episode 27 will air in the future is undecided.
"Sugochikku Mirorin" is an anime depicting the daily life of magical girl Mirorin, popular with both children and adults. This is its 15th season.

entries.en: Following the giant creature incidents in Miyato City, the professional baseball organizing body announced that games will be canceled for the time being. It says the appearance of giant creatures is unpredictable and the safety of spectators and staff cannot be guaranteed. Cancellations will continue until it is judged safe to hold games.

Mr. A, a self-employed person who was nearly blown away by the powerful wind, said, "Because I was hiding behind something, I escaped a direct hit from the wind. I saw people blown away like dead leaves. It was terrifying."

entries.en:
O. R. James, author of the mega-hit novel "The Tale of the Last Sword," announced on the official website a charity sale to support Miyato City, where giant creatures appeared.
The sale covers "The Tale of the Last Sword" series in a special binding. Buyers can freely set the amount, starting from 1,000 yen. James said, "Even little candies become a great source of strength when many are gathered. Please lend Miyato City a little of your strength."

entries.en:
It has come to light that "Ristorante Miyato," with its main restaurant in Yotsuba Ward, Miyato City, will close. The restaurant is a popular high-end French restaurant in Miyato City that had expanded overseas, but its management has recently changed, and it aims to reopen as a new eatery under a different business policy.
According to David, said to be the head chef of the new restaurant, "Drawing on our excellent knowledge and experience of French cuisine, we're planning a members-only restaurant that will delight gourmets, combining it with udon, kishimen, and rice bowls."
The main restaurant will be closed for a while. The building will be renovated, and the overseas branches will be wound down. The new restaurant's opening date is still undecided.

entries.en: Miyato City's Ristorante Miyato Doing Well Overseas

entries.en:
It has come to light that the overseas branches of "Ristorante Miyato," with its main restaurant in Yotsuba Ward, Miyato City, are doing well and are expected to reach their annual sales target of 500 million yen. The restaurant is popular as a high-end French restaurant.
It has long been eager to expand abroad, operating more than 10 restaurants in North America, Europe, Asia, and elsewhere. An industry insider said, "The food is delicious, of course, but the service is well suited to each country's culture. It's also active in cultural exchange; apparently you can dine while listening to performances of other countries' instruments or rakugo."

entries.en:
Shortly after 6:00 p.m. on April 3, two giant aliens about 40 meters tall appeared near the Marugame intersection on National Route 3 in Minami-Shinjuku 9-chome, Shinjuku Ward, and began fighting. The two giants fought using optical weapons and martial arts.

According to Mr. Tomisaka, a Tama City resident who watched the fight up close, the two looked very much alike when they first appeared, but after one of them fell on its backside onto an overpass, its appearance changed.

The glowing giant whose appearance did not change reportedly had part of the center of its chest flashing, then soared into the sky and flew away at high speed.
Afterward, the remaining one destroyed the city, apparently injuring several hundred people.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0167.json:p0/k56; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The giant alien that disguised itself as the giant of light and destroyed the city called itself Alien Zarab and stated that it had come to Earth from planet Zarab to establish friendly relations with Earth.
It is estimated to be about 40 meters tall and weigh about 20,000 tons.
Alien Zarab first appeared in Shinjuku Ward looking almost exactly like the giant of light (Ultraman), and kept destroying nearby buildings and cars with a weapon called the "Energy Vulcan" fired from its fingertips.
Ultraman forced it to reveal its true form, showing that the attacker had been Alien Zarab.

Several mysteries remain, such as why Alien Zarab, which came to build friendly relations, destroyed the city.
Mr. Watanabe (pseudonym), an office worker who commutes to the area from Kawasaki City, angrily said, "I trusted Alien Zarab, so I'm very disappointed. Why did it disguise itself as Ultraman and destroy the city? If the goal was to ruin Ultraman's reputation, that's unforgivable."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0167.json:p0/k60; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
A burglar broke into the Tonchigi police box in Minami-Shinjuku and stole one policewoman's uniform. According to police, the break-in occurred while officers were guiding evacuations when the giant aliens appeared in the city.
The culprit broke the door of the reception room and stole the uniform from a wardrobe in the break room. Police are treating it as a theft and collecting eyewitness information.

Sergeant Horiuchi, who was at the police box at the time, said while spitting with fervor, "I didn't notice the door being broken at all. This must be the work of aliens. Why would aliens steal Officer Ishida's policewoman uniform? It's an outrage!"

The stolen item is a policewoman's uniform in size M. According to its owner, Officer Ishida, it was brand new as of last week.
To the thief, Officer Ishida said, "Losing a policewoman's uniform causes all kinds of trouble, so please give it back. If you return it, I'll give you a different private costume in exchange."

entries.en:
Police announced that passersby found hundreds of high-denomination bills fluttering through the air near the Marugame intersection on National Route 3 in Minami-Shinjuku 9-chome, Shinjuku Ward, and turned them in as lost property.

The scene is where the giant aliens were fighting at the time, and the bills are believed to have come out of a building after the aliens destroyed it.

So far, no one has come forward as the owner. The fact that no owner has stepped forward despite so much money being scattered has fueled speculation that it may be the kind of money that can't be shown in public.

entries.en:
Major convenience store chain Green Green announced that its fried chicken sales for the March quarter rose to 160% of the previous year.

The company's fried chicken comes in a wide range of flavors such as soy sauce, milk, and strawberry, as well as dessert-style varieties, making it popular with women too. The company is eager to keep offering innovative fried chicken that incorporates customer feedback.

Among fans, many posts speculate about the company's next fried chicken lineup, such as "Next up is marinated tuna flavor" and "It's got to be a dessert. If so, tiramisu fried chicken is very likely next," stirring up strange expectations.

entries.en:
Around 6:00 p.m. on April 3, a G-Z Transit bus nearly caught up in the fight between giant aliens in Minami-Shinjuku was able to evacuate all of its passengers safely thanks to the quick thinking of driver Yoichi Tawarada.

Passenger Mr. Fujita, a Maihama resident, said, "We were almost stepped on by a giant foot, but the driver controlled the bus skillfully and we got out safely. And the driver stayed on the bus guiding everyone until we'd all evacuated. He saved our lives."

entries.en: The GZOE Building in Minami-Shinjuku 8-chome was destroyed by a giant alien. The alien reportedly thrust a huge hand into the building and threw the office into chaos with a telekinesis-like power.

entries.en:
Motoko Tomii of Shinjuku Ward, who sold flowers on the street, had her shop destroyed by crowds fleeing in panic from the giant alien attack.
Ms. Tomii's shop was well regarded by customers for her loving care of flowers, and was always busy with customers buying flowers on their way home from work.

Watching the shop she had cherished for thirty years being crushed before her eyes, Ms. Tomii was so shocked that she crouched down and couldn't move.

Mr. Sasaki, a regular customer living in Kamata who happened to witness the scene, said while rubbing his right elbow and shoulder, "People fleeing crashed into Ms. Tomii's stall one after another. The stall held up through the first two times, but when it was hit the third time, it was completely crushed. They were crashing into it with considerable force, so there's no way the stall could have held up. It's truly a pity."

We hope Ms. Tomii recovers and reopens her flower shop.

entries.en:
Clear umbrellas are now booming among women in their twenties, mainly in metropolitan areas. Clear umbrellas used to be generally seen as cheap, but this year major department stores and apparel makers have one after another introduced brand-name and designer-supervised clear umbrellas and offered variations with finely selectable levels of transparency, apparently winning over female customers.

Akiko Watanuki, a trading company employee living in Tokyo, said, "I love the sheer clarity of clear umbrellas. On rainy days, when I watch the rain dripping through the umbrella, my gloom clears up and I feel refreshed! I have about 20 clear umbrellas with different transparencies. I pick how transparent an umbrella to take depending on my mood that day."

The clear umbrella boom looks set to continue.

entries.en:
An investigation by the National Police Agency has revealed that Sergeant Horiuchi and Officer Ishida of the Tonchigi police box, under the jurisdiction of Minami-Shinjuku Station, had been growing vegetables for their own consumption on state-owned land behind the police box.
Horiuchi and Ishida reportedly grew vegetables they liked, such as snow peas and cherry tomatoes, and served them at their own meals nearly every night. Some also believe they even used fertilizer, seriously aiming to increase their harvest.

When questioned, Sergeant Horiuchi reportedly said, "I just really wanted one more dish at dinner. At first I started casually, thinking just green onions would be fine. Gradually it escalated, and I got into seasonal vegetables like spinach and snow peas. Once I started growing cherry tomatoes, there was no stopping me. I am truly sorry to the citizens and my fellow officers."

Taking the matter seriously, the National Police Agency intends to tighten controls by adding a ban on home gardens behind police boxes to its work regulations. Sergeant Horiuchi received a three-month pay cut, and Officer Ishida a one-month pay cut.

entries.en:
One of the flying creatures that appeared above the Sky Garden Bridge.
At first glance, it looks like a moth grown to giant size. Could it be a mutation?
However, Dr. Shionogi, an expert in animal research, disagrees: "Mutations can make things larger, but in Lepidoptera there are only records confirming sizes up to 32 centimeters. And even if an Earth creature grew giant through mutation, at the size seen this time, flight would be impossible given its body structure. At this point, all I can say is that it's not a creature of this Earth."

Part of what is thought to be tissue from this flying creature has been found at sea, and a special project to study it is to be launched. The doctor is eager to take part.

entries.en:
We have obtained footage of a Garden Liner car right after the accident, filmed on a cell phone by Shizuo Sato (pseudonym), who miraculously survived the collapse of the Sky Garden Bridge.

It is clear that the car has come completely off the rails and cannot run.
Several people also appear in the footage, but unfortunately there are still no reports that they survived.

The collapse of the Sky Garden Bridge has had a virtually fatal impact on Garden Liner operations.
Katsuzo Hinokaji (62), president of GR, which operates the Garden Liner, squeezed out the words with a haggard expression: "With the bridge gone, restoration is impossible at this point."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k136; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
An astonishing discovery has been made from the footage of Shizuo Sato (pseudonym), who miraculously survived.
It showed the culprit of the mass killing at West Azami Park about two months ago.

"Ah! It's this face!" one of the officers examining the cell phone footage, submitted to understand the situation on the bridge, suddenly cried out. Officer Akira Fukiishi (28) says his efforts paid off: he had saved the wanted criminal's mugshot on his own phone and looked at it morning and night to burn it into his memory.

Unfortunately, the suspect's survival has not been confirmed since the bridge collapsed. We sincerely hope the day will come when the officer's efforts are rewarded with an "arrest."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k138; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
It has come to light that a motorcycle owned by Shizuo Sato (pseudonym), who miraculously survived the collapse of the Sky Garden Bridge, was stolen.

At the time, Sato (pseudonym) was riding his motorcycle on the bridge when he encountered the giant creature attack, and while stranded, the stress gave him an upset stomach. He walked to a place where he wouldn't bother anyone, relieved himself, and when he came back, the motorcycle had vanished without a trace.

According to people nearby, a young couple hopped on the motorcycle before anyone could stop them and headed east.
To begin with, it's common sense not to drive cars and such in an emergency. Furthermore, one can't help but question the ethics of using someone else's property without permission, even to save your own life.

That said, in running this article, we heard quite a few voices saying things like "If they didn't know who the owner was, they couldn't even say a word, could they?" and "I understand putting yourself first when your life is in danger."
This debate looks set to go on for a long time.

entries.en: A Phone Over Your Life?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k151; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Our reporting has revealed that Kanae Shimizu (20) (pseudonym), who was thrown into the sea in the collapse of the Sky Garden Bridge but rescued, did something astonishing when she came to.
She passed out when she was thrown into the sea and was pulled out onto the nearby shore. Her parents were able to rush over just then and rejoiced that their only beloved daughter had survived. Wrapped in a blanket, she woke up in her parents' arms and looked back and forth between their faces for a while. Her memory seemed to have gone blank from around when she fell off the bridge, and when her parents explained what had happened, she nodded again and again as if remembering. Just when it seemed "all's well that ends well," she began searching her pockets and surroundings for her cell phone, ignoring her dumbfounded parents and the rescue workers around her. "My phone, my phone's gone." Her parents tried to calm her as she searched desperately, saying, "You can just buy another one," but for some reason she was fixated on the phone she'd had, and finally even started trying to dive into the sea herself.
Thanks to the quick action of the rescue workers, they managed to stop her from jumping in, but she is reportedly still fixated on that phone at the hospital she was taken to. Even her parents don't know why.　This writer is now intensely curious and hopes to bring you a follow-up at a later date.

entries.en: The Bus That Saved a Life
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k153; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Shizuo Sato (pseudonym), who took many valuable photos on the collapsing Sky Garden Bridge, reportedly owes his narrow escape from death to a bus that happened to be nearby when it collapsed.
Sato instantly jumped into the bus, sat in a seat, took a brace position like in an emergency landing, and grabbed the pipe of the seat in front of him.
The bus fell into the sea along with chunks of steel and concrete that had once been the bridge. Underwater, one piece of steel and concrete after another came crashing in, and the bus was dented all over. Protected by the bus's steel armor, Sato was able to survive until things around him settled down.
There was more good luck. Sato had a 2-liter plastic bottle, but he had already finished it and it was empty.
This apparently let him survive underwater longer than usual.
Who could have predicted that the spirit of not littering would come in handy in a place like this?

So there's no misunderstanding: staying inside a vehicle is not always the right thing to do. There are plenty of risks, such as being unable to get out because of water pressure if it's sealed, or getting pinned inside and unable to move.

entries.en: Scoop on the Motorcycle Thieves?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k155; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Just before the Sky Garden Bridge's final major collapse, our news helicopter captured intriguing footage.
It shows the moment two people on a motorcycle make a movie-like giant jump. For a moment it looked like a spectacular escape from the collapsing bridge, but the motorcycle looked familiar.
According to our in-house video analysis, the motorcycle the two are riding is the same model and color as the one reported stolen.
If so, doesn't that make this footage of the thieves?
Because it was shot at extreme telephoto, identifying faces is very difficult, but we are providing it to the police and independently continuing further video analysis. Stay tuned for updates.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k156; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
As the giant flying creatures rampaged on the Sky Garden Bridge, among those stranded along with this writer was a nurse.
She said she always carries simple medical supplies, and she did everything she could to treat people, such as giving a compress to someone who had hurt their back.
Having experienced numerous disaster sites firsthand, this writer knows well that a person's true nature comes out in an emergency like this.
Afterward, the Sky Garden Bridge collapsed, and sadly, this woman is still missing.
I earnestly hope she survived.
(Written by Sudo)

entries.en:
A woman cowering and trembling as giant flying creatures flew around overhead.
When I spoke to her, she repeated like a mantra, "I just want to go home."
It's a common sight, how people act when faced with terror they can do nothing about, in a place with no escape.
Fortunately, she survived the bridge collapse, though she suffered injuries including fractures.
The sight of her crying in her parents' arms in her hospital room warmed this writer's heart too.　(Written by Sudo)

entries.en:
With the train destroyed and the collapsed bridge blocking the way, I encountered someone trying to sell products to meet his sales quota.

People who stay calm in an emergency like this are rare. Even this writer, who has experienced many disasters, has almost never met one.
I was intrigued and talked with him, and it made sense. Not disasters, but he had spent many years posted in countries where conflicts were taking place. That must be what gave him nerves of steel.

Unfortunately, he has been missing since the bridge collapsed. Yet I can't shake the feeling that he's alive somewhere.
(Written by Sudo)
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k190; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
On the Sky Garden Bridge, as collapse loomed, some people complained of physical problems or feeling unwell.
The man in this footage apparently hurt his back when he was thrown from the destroyed train.
At first it was just a slight discomfort, he says, but the pain grew stronger as time went on.

It's very dangerous to leave it alone because "it's an emergency," "it's just a scratch," or "it only hurts a little."
If you're not constantly on the move and can spare even a little time, and if you have any means of treatment, even first aid, you should do it.

Fortunately, this man was able to get a compress and became able to walk, if slowly.
If a "what if" situation ever happens to you, I'd be glad if you remembered this article. (Written by Sudo)
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k192; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
There was a man who said he had twisted his ankle and couldn't move.
But it was actually a lie; apparently he wanted to avoid having to risk danger and take the lead in trying to escape.
This time it didn't have much of a bad effect, but lies like this often cause great trouble for those around them.
That's because they take away valuable medicine and the time of doctors and nurses. That can lead to people who truly need treatment not getting it.

Afterward, he survived, but apparently broke both legs in the bridge collapse and the fall into the sea. (Written by Sudo)
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k194; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
It's also a common sight to see people looking around frantically, not knowing what's happening or what to do in a sudden emergency.
Their minds go into a panic, and they can't even think of taking a deep breath to calm down.
In such cases, care is needed, because clumsy attempts by others to calm them down can actually make them more upset. (Written by Sudo)
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k196; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
As the Sky Garden Bridge drew close to collapse, I came across a truly disappointing person.
What was so disappointing was what he muttered to himself, which I couldn't help overhearing.
He was apparently scheming to escape alone while the giant flying creatures were busy attacking other people.
It can't be helped that one's own safety comes first. But even so, what kind of person plans on the premise of others' sacrifice?

This writer once met, in another disaster, a person who would not hesitate to kill others to survive.
It's truly disappointing.

Since the bridge collapsed, he remains missing. (Written by Sudo)

entries.en:
This footage captures the moment the upper roadway was destroyed by a giant flying creature's beam, and rubble collapsed onto the lower level along with the cars that had been on the upper level.
At the time, the scene was in a state of emergency where people were trapped by rubble and couldn't escape, even though similar destruction could have happened anywhere on the bridge at any moment.

When the bridge is rebuilt, I hope to see facilities like ladders that let stranded people get down to the water so they can escape. It may not be giant creatures next time, but there's no denying a similar situation could arise from an earthquake or other disaster. (Written by Sudo)
