entries.en:
Before the bridge restaurant collapsed, I was able to capture the scene where part of the restaurant fell away.
The floor tilted, and chairs and tables slid down the slanted floor and fell into the sea.
These sliding chairs and tables are a real nuisance.

In fact, this writer has encountered a similar situation before.
That time, I managed to avoid falling into the sea by instantly hanging from the edge of the floor.
I thought I'd rarely see such a sight, but apparently not.

If you ever encounter this, don't panic: keep an eye on where the sliding chairs and tables are,
and try to run up to a part of the floor that isn't tilted so you don't get hit. (Written by Sudo)

entries.en:
Do you know the name Tatsujiro Koshiba?
It is the name of the founder of COCYBA, a manufacturer and seller of toilet and kitchen products that now boasts a 99% share in Japan and a 70% share overseas.

He was once an apprentice of the great master Shunzo Sanuki.
But while Sanuki was strongly inclined to be an artist who crafted each piece one by one, Koshiba wanted to "make things that are beautiful and serve their purpose, yet are cheap enough for many people to use," and so he parted ways with Sanuki.

Then, with a small amount of money and funds borrowed using his home as collateral, he founded "Koshiba Co., Ltd."
This "Koshiba Co., Ltd." would later become "COCYBA."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k214; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Of the things he had learned under Sanuki, Koshiba first decided to manufacture and sell toilets.
Western-style ones, rare at the time.
Koshiba poured his heart and soul into creating the original toilet that served as the mold, and mass-produced toilets from it.

Koshiba's toilets, better designed and cheaper than those on the market until then, were welcomed by the public and quickly spread nationwide.
Yet Koshiba's spirits were reportedly at rock bottom.
Around the time mass production began, Koshiba visited the home of his former master Sanuki to have him look at the product.
On seeing the toilet, Sanuki was furious and smashed it against a garden stone.
Even if the original Koshiba had made was a masterpiece, mass production inevitably creates differences between individual units.
To Sanuki, that made them all something else entirely, already defective products lacking balance.

Though the public recognized him and sales kept climbing, Sanuki's words pierced Koshiba's heart.
That's because Sanuki had seen right through the fact that he was compromising on the beauty of form for the sake of mass production.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k216; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
After that, Koshiba built a research facility and, together with his workers, began working day and night to build a mass-production system that would reproduce the original.
With the president holed up in the lab, the company couldn't run. During that time, the one who ran the company as vice president was Koshiba's wife, Shizuka.

Even though male dominance was taken for granted back then, Shizuka showed fierce leadership and grew the company even larger.

And after five years holed up in the lab, Koshiba finally succeeded in building a system that produced mass-produced goods exactly like the original.
Sanuki, on seeing these mass-produced goods, didn't say so, but apparently approved of them; they are still installed in Sanuki's toilet today.

Five years of grueling, intense research took its toll on the workers' bodies, and half of those who took part died of what we would now call overwork.
However, they had supported Koshiba's vision during their lives and proudly told family and friends they were doing it willingly; indeed, no one sued after their deaths.
Not only that, but they didn't accept any memorial money from the company. Accepting it, they said, would go against their pride.

Koshiba, too, passed away two days after having Sanuki look at the product.
His expression was said to be very peaceful.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0168.json:p0/k222; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
How many people can instantly picture a "windsock" when they hear the word?
A "windsock" is a tube-shaped cloth often seen on roads and at airports. Some may recognize it if I say it's the one with green and white stripes, or orange and white stripes.
It is installed so you can tell the rough direction and strength of the wind.
People driving their own cars may not pay much attention to it, but it's very useful in places like coastal roads, where strong winds can easily cause accidents.
In that kind of weather, windows are usually closed tight, making it hard to grasp the situation.

Incidentally, it came in handy for this writer during a disaster once.
That time, I had to cross a steel beam where walls and floors had collapsed in an earthquake, but a nearby windsock let me know when gusts were coming,
and as a result I was able to cross without being blown off the beam by a gust.
I recommend making a habit of paying attention to the things around you. (Written by Sudo)

entries.en:
＜1. Purple Flashes Across the Sky!＞
Many of you have probably seen purple flashes in the sky over the past few days.
These flashes have been sighted worldwide, mainly in the Northern Hemisphere, and astronomers and
space and weather research institutions in many countries are investigating, but their true nature has yet to be revealed.
Our editorial team interviewed Deputy Director Sasaki of the National Cosmic Ray Research Institute about the flashes.
(The National Cosmic Ray Research Institute is an organization that studies the various high-energy radiation
traveling through space.)

Reporter: What are those purple flashes?
Deputy Director: We don't know yet. They may be a type of weather phenomenon, but they have little in common
　　　　with the various weather phenomena observed so far, so the institute is skeptical of that theory.
　　　　Perhaps they are some other unknown luminous phenomenon. (Continued on next page)
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r26/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
＜1. Purple Flashes Across the Sky!＞
(Continued from previous page)
Reporter: What effects do the flashes have on the human body?
Deputy Director: So far, there have been no reports of anyone suffering physical or mental problems from exposure to the purple light.
　　　　Radiation levels are also no different from normal. However, because they suddenly flash purple,
　　　　there do seem to have been cases of people being startled or distracted and having accidents.

Reporter: How will you respond to the flashes going forward?
Deputy Director: The institute will continue investigating the flashes.
　　　　We hope to move the investigation forward as quickly as possible.

The true nature of the purple flashes is unknown, but for now it seems that worrying about them too much and getting distracted
is the greater danger. New information is eagerly awaited.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r26/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
＜2. The Much-Talked-About Iberis Tower Building: Popular Gourmet Spots＞
The "Iberis Tower Building," a high-rise built in the bay area overlooking the Sky Garden Bridge,
is a popular spot with a panoramic view of Miyato City from its observation room.
B2 to 15F are the shopping area, 16F to 26F the office area,
and 27F to 48F the hotel area.
The most popular part of the tower right now is the gourmet floors on 14F and 15F,
home to all kinds of restaurants. Famous restaurants from all over the country have opened here, making it hard to choose,
but this time we'll introduce "Pizzeria Bellano," the most popular with women in their twenties.

The pizzas baked by a pizza chef who trained in Naples itself have a perfect balance of salt and char in the crust
and are delicious. Our recommendation is the Margherita with genuine mozzarella made from water buffalo milk.
Be sure to enjoy it with the house-recommended wine.
Also popular is the challenge menu item, the "Galaxy Mountain Mille-Feuille Pizza," with every kind of pizza on the menu stacked like a mille-feuille,
weighing 2 kg in total.
Finish it within 30 minutes and your meal is free!
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r26/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
＜3. Interview: "My Diary"＞　Risa Kashiwagi (Journalist)
In this edition of "My Diary," we talk with journalist Risa Kashiwagi.

Reporter: You're known for your striking reportage on young people's behavioral psychology and how they
　　　　express themselves in their social lives, and you're active across many media.
　　　　You're also good at sports, speak seven languages, and are said to cook at a professional level.
　　　　How does someone as talented as you come to be?
　　　　First, may I ask what led you to become a journalist?
Risa Kashiwagi (Kashiwagi): In high school, because of my parents' work, I had the chance to live abroad.
　　　　That's when I learned that there were worlds with completely different languages and customs.
　　　　After that, I became interested in the culture and customs of my own country too.
　　　　I think that led to my current work. (Continued on next page)
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r26/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
＜3. Interview: "My Diary"＞　Risa Kashiwagi (Journalist)
(Continued from previous page)
Reporter: You started working as a journalist right after entering university, didn't you?
Kashiwagi: Back then, it had already become normal for ordinary people to put out information online.
　　　　But I think I was lucky that so many people recognized my work.
Reporter: What activities do you have planned going forward?
Kashiwagi: I've been doing a lot of reporting in Japan lately, but I want to somehow make time
　　　　to go report abroad. Also, I'd like to go swimming this summer.
　　　　Oh, and also
Reporter: What is it?
Kashiwagi: My cooking isn't professional level. It's just average (laughs).
Reporter: Pardon us (laughs). Thank you for your time today.

entries.en:
＜4. The Suspicious Ties Between Officials and a Certain Organization＞
Our editorial team has learned of a place that an official of a certain ministry has been frequenting for the past few years.
It is the Fortune Center Building in Yotsuba Ward, Miyato City. The official has visited this building,
which houses the offices of various companies, many times. When we confirmed by phone with each ministry,
we were told, "There is no such fact." They aren't hiding it;
they probably really don't know. The official is likely concealing their position and visiting
in secret.
We have another piece of information: that a defense official gave preferential treatment to a certain Company A
in equipment procurement and bidding (preferential treatment here meaning the official personally took under-the-table money
and leaked bidding information). However, Company A does not have an office in the Fortune Center
Building. Our suspicion is that something connecting the defense official and Company A
lies in this Fortune Center Building.
This matter is still under investigation. We will report as soon as we have solid information.
Stay tuned. (Editor-in-Chief: Hirai)

entries.en:
【The Mechanism of Gigantism in Deep-Sea Creatures】
　　　　　　　　　　　　　Professor Hitomi Fukazawa, Miyato University

It is said that "the deep sea is farther away than outer space." Even with the latest survey equipment, research on it
is still in its early stages, and much remains unknown. Here, I'd like to introduce one of my research
themes: "gigantism in deep-sea creatures."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r30/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The giant squid, which has been sighted more often recently, the Japanese spider crab, the world's largest arthropod,
and the oarfish, which can reach 10 m in length, are all creatures living in the so-called "deep sea,"
at depths of 200 m or more. Not just these three: many creatures living in the deep sea are large
compared to those living in shallow waters (the surface zone).
The deep sea differs from the surface zone in its environment: sunlight doesn't reach it and water pressure is high,
and the creatures living there have developed unusual forms. Gigantism is thought to be one of the ways
they survive.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r30/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
There are various theories as to why deep-sea creatures grow large, but
　1. Growing large makes them less likely to be eaten by predators
　2. A large body can store more nutrients, making it easier to survive in the deep sea, where prey is scarce
　3. In water they are less affected by gravity, so their bodies are easier to support even when large
are among the reasons considered.
Of course, much of the deep sea is unknown, so these reasons are not the whole story.
It would be no surprise if there were deep-sea creatures whose size and ecology are beyond our imagination.
(It is to meet such creatures that we researchers continue our work.)

The dependable cop that everyone admired as a child...

A costume with enough appeal to change the course of someone's life:

Police uniforms come in many forms.
There are uniforms for men and for women, differences by season such as summer uniforms,

According to the Cosplay White Paper, the most popular of all police uniforms

Special Feature【Welcome! Fast-Food Workers!】

As a student, don't you remember being soothed or getting butterflies
from the fresh smile of a fast-food worker?
One acquaintance of mine even says, "I wanted to see that uniform and smile, so I
kept going to the restaurant until I'd conquered the entire secret menu."

This issue's feature is the leading everyday cosplay: fast-food workers!

The appeal of the fast-food worker uniform lies in how highly it achieves various qualities like
"approachability," "cleanliness," "modesty," and "flair." Also, uniforms actually used in restaurants
excel not only in design but also in function, such as
being "easy to put on and take off," "stain-resistant," and "durable,"
and another key point is that they're made to fire you up, like

Why not dare to cosplay as a fast-food worker precisely when you're feeling a little down?

The bright, positive costume will lift your mood,
and you might find yourself smiling a lovely smile...!

Heroes who spring into action amid raging flames to save people...!

That's firefighters. Along with police officers, they're popular as the costume of

One acquaintance of mine even says,

When you wear turnout gear, its toughness makes you feel

But while turnout gear is heat-resistant, that doesn't mean you should

entries.en:
Tonight the Horuho Cedar Forest is restless.
Standing on a cliff overlooking the game trail that ran along the mountainside, Naran touched the dagger at his waist.
Touching this blade, a keepsake of his father, always seemed to restore his courage and composure.
He set his footing and nocked an arrow to his bow with practiced hands.

He had been summoned so suddenly that he'd forgotten his cloak.
The kiranaria flowers would bloom soon, but the nights were still cold.
He could see flames rising from the southern settlement. Naran knit his still-youthful brows.
Ophir's vanguard, no doubt. He thought of Mars, whom he'd often played with as a child.
Mars should have been living in that settlement.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
But he couldn't clearly recall his face.
With elven blood in his veins, Naran lived far longer than the villagers.
If Mars were alive, he'd be about 150 by now.

Thinking himself heartless, he still felt that he had to delay "them"
from reaching the village, if only a little.
Elena was in the village.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Naran's slightly pointed ears twitched. From deep along the game trail below came the presence of many people.
Not people, precisely. Monsters controlled by Ophir, the sorcerer of the "Seventh Tower."

Large armored pigs walked noisily on two legs.
It seemed to be a unit of about ten orcs.
Each held a different weapon as they jostled their way along the game trail.
Up close they stank horribly. Naran grimaced at the memory.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"Too few... It can't be helped."

Muttering this, Naran drew his bow and loosed an arrow in a seemingly wrong direction.
The arrow flew lightly through the air, took on a glow, and pierced a rock jutting out from the cliff.
A magic arrow.
When the arrow gave off a faint light, the rock cracked and rained down on the pigs on the game trail.
When the roaring cloud of dust settled, the game trail fell silent.
The orc unit seemed to have been wiped out.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"Two left. Nowhere near enough."

Naran slung his bow on his back and ran toward the village.
On the way, Keen, who had also gone out to intercept them, joined him.

"Naran, the southern settlement's been crushed! What are they after? Food, after all?"
"Who knows, but I doubt it's food."
"Treasure?"
"There's no treasure in the village. Not that I know of, anyway."
"What, and you call yourself an elf?"
"Even at my age, there's more I don't know than I do."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Naran knew that Ophir was after the "Sage's Green Stone."
The village had something like a legend about it, but it had become like a fairy tale, and no one knew where it was.
Naran had come to this village with his father in search of the green stone, and for two generations they had searched for it while serving as something like the village's bodyguards.
He had a rough idea of where it was, but he wasn't sure.

But to Naran now, life with the villagers mattered more than the green stone.

"Elena..."

When he murmured this and glanced to the side with a start, Keen was grinning.
An honest, quick-witted young man.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
They reached the village. The orcs hadn't come yet.
Naran rushed to the well at the edge of the village, where he suspected the green stone was hidden.
There was no sign it had been disturbed. But once Ophir came, it would soon be found.
Before that...

At that moment, a sword pierced Naran's chest. Keen had stabbed him from behind.

"Thanks for showing me the way. So this is where it was."

Keen's silhouette blurred and became the figure of a middle-aged sorcerer. Ophir.
Naran collapsed on the spot. Blood poured from his chest. In his fading vision, Ophir was casting a detection spell.
It's over. The Sage's Green Stone...
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Just then, someone shook Naran hard.
Regaining a sliver of consciousness, he heavily opened his eyelids. It was Keen.

"Naran! Are you all right?! I can't believe they got you!"
"You don't need to worry anymore. I'm finished."
"I'll treat you right now!"
"Well, do as you like. More importantly..."

Naran handed the dagger at his waist to Keen.
"I'm sorry, but I leave the rest to you."
With that, Naran looked up at the sky and quietly drew his last breath.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 1: Chapter of the Past" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r42/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Since then, he had fled for his life and was now in pitch-black darkness.
Through the pitch-black void, the seven-headed white horse carrying him pressed on.
The light its white body gave off was swallowed by the deep darkness, and no one could see it.

The white-hulled space cruiser Uchchaihshravas had been traveling through the pitch-black darkness for two full weeks in Earth time.
The windows of the command room, on the middle level of the bridge, were pitch-black walls, as if the defense shutters were closed.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r43/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en: He... Vice Admiral Momihog, the protagonist of this story, is an unreliable soldier known as "the Torture Admiral."\nLooking at the unchanging windows, Momihog recalled the battle fought two weeks ago at the space fortress in Pluto's orbit.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r43/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en: After a year and a half of large-scale fighting in the solar system, the Granzella Reform Army had been forced to shrink its front lines before the overwhelming national power of the Earth Unified Army, and had holed up in the space fortress on Pluto, but even that was taken two weeks ago.\n\nThe Pluto Base Garrison led by Vice Admiral Momihog packed as many soldiers as they could onto a few space vessels, and somehow managed to escape toward outer space using the railgun catapult installed at the space fortress.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r43/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en: Momihog was thinking. Of a way to retake the solar system with these few vessels.\nA head-on clash with the Earth Unified Army would be hopeless. They were sorely lacking in both vessels and the dimensional fighters they carried.\nUnable to settle on an idea, he stabbed his fork into a half-eaten chiffon cake and stuffed it into his mouth, and at that very moment his adjutant, Major Miyoko G. Lazarov, spoke up.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r43/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"Admiral Momihog, several ship silhouettes at three o'clock! They're not transmitting friendly identification signals!"
The command room was thrown into an uproar.
(Have they beaten us to it...?)
Momihog loosened the collar of his uniform
and looked up at the large screen hanging from the command room ceiling.

The screen showed the space off the starboard side.
He could see particles of light welling up in the darkness.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r43/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The light welling up in the darkness spread left and right in an instant, deploying as if to surround
Momihog's vessels.

In a pitch-black subspace shifted 0.5 dimensions from normal space,
the white-hulled space cruiser Uchchaihshravas went to battle stations.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 2: Chapter of Pitch Darkness" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r43/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
A lot had happened since then, and Keen had been walking for three days and three nights. But no matter how far he went, he found no town or village, and at last his food and water ran out.

Keen was gripped by fierce hunger, and was even half ready to give up, thinking this might be the end.
Still, after walking a while longer, he found an old man wrapped in rags standing in the road like a ghost.
When Keen asked whether there was a town or village nearby, the old man feebly pointed deep into the forest
and muttered, "A village..."
Keen nodded his thanks and went into the forest.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The forest was thick with trees and undergrowth that blocked Keen's way. Was there really a village in a place like this?
Keen grew more and more uneasy.
Still, he somehow kept going, and when it had grown completely dark, he found a large lake deep in the forest.
Moonlight fell on the lake and rippled on its surface, and he gazed at the moon in the lake for a while. Something seemed to be floating there, but his hunger brought him back to his senses, and he hurriedly looked around.
But no matter how much he searched, he couldn't find the village.

Had he lost his way, or had the old man tricked him? His hunger was nearing its limit,
but he had no choice but to turn back here.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
It was a little while after he left the lake.
From somewhere drifted a smell like soup or some other food.
So there was a village around here after all?
He followed the smell, and for some reason found himself back at the lake.

But there stood a village that hadn't been there a moment ago.
He wondered if he was seeing an illusion, but there was certainly a small village, with about five houses of various sizes lined up, flat and mushroom-like, with chimneys.
It seemed strange, but above all he was relieved to be saved.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Light spilled from the windows of the houses, but he couldn't see well inside.
In any case, to ask for some food, he headed for the entrance of the biggest house.

He called out loudly to ask if anyone was there, but there was no answer. When he knocked, the door creaked open,
and the smell of food drifted out from inside.

He felt a little guilty, but Keen decided to go inside.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Even after entering, he shouted to see if anyone was there, but again there was no answer.
What was stranger was that, though the house was full of the smell of food, it was completely empty inside.
He walked around for a while, but it seemed to be a single room with no stairs or anything.
Looking closely, he saw something lying in the corner of the room.

Keen picked it up.
It was unmistakably a human bone.
And the next moment, the house began to shake violently.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Sensing danger, he turned around, but the door had vanished before he knew it.
The house shook violently, and he even felt it moving sideways.

Nearly falling over, he stabbed his sword into the wall to get out.

The feel of the sword going in was strange.
The wall had an odd springiness, softer than it looked, and from where he'd stabbed, a thick, dark red liquid came flowing out.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
This house was a living creature.
It mimicked a house and lured prey in with smells to eat them.
It was that kind of creature.

Keen kept driving his sword into the wall.
Then a hole opened, and this time clear water came gushing out.
The room was filling with water fast, so he forced the hole wider and got out.

Outside was underwater. It seemed he was in the lake.
The creature sank to the bottom of the lake.
But when he strained his eyes, the other houses were floating, swaying, beneath the lake's surface.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
When Keen climbed onto the shore, the village had completely vanished. What had been chimneys poked out of the lake's surface. Did they breathe through those?

Keen hurried back to the old man.
But all that lay there were rags and bones.
On a whim, he fit the bone he'd picked up in the house against them, and it matched perfectly in size.

It had been a strange experience, but Keen's hunger was nearing its limit.
When he slowly took a bite of the house's flesh he'd cut off, a taste just like soup filled his mouth.
With a strange sense of satisfaction, Keen set off on his journey once more.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 3: Chapter of Famine" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r44/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
After that, Keen arrived at a port town.
It was to rest his body, worn out from a long journey.
For Keen, who had done nothing but fight, his time in the port town was a brief moment of peace.

But Keen had one more reason for visiting this town.
To win the tournament at the town's arena, and to obtain the royal family's treasured shield, given to the warrior who is recognized.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Holding the royal family's treasured shield is also proof of being the strongest, so mighty warriors from all over the world
gather at the arena.

For Keen, who wanted to know his own strength and to fight strong opponents, the arena was a dream stage.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The next day, the battle at the arena finally began.

The rules were a one-on-one tournament format, and any weapons or armor were allowed.
Besides humans, many races took part, including trolls, centaurs, and birdfolk.
All kinds of mighty warriors had gathered, from those who fought with swordsmanship and weapons like Keen to those who used magic.

His blood boiling before so many mighty foes, Keen took his beloved blazing sword "Ragun Raaze" in hand and stepped onto the stage of battle.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Keen defeated one powerful opponent after another in the first and second rounds, advancing through the tournament.

The movements of the flaming tip of the blazing sword "Ragun Raaze" could not be read by ordinary fighters.
Yes, the blazing sword, too, had overcome a string of hardships alongside Keen to get here.
The blazing sword was answering the burning passion of Keen, who had endured so much over so long.

I want to be stronger.
No one could stop Keen, who had sought power with that wish in his heart.
Watching the flame swordsman's overwhelming winning streak, not a single spectator doubted Keen would win.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The feast of battle was finally down to its last match.
Keen had at last made it to the final.
His opponent in the final was a boy a size smaller than Keen,
but Keen was startled when he saw the crimson sword the boy held.

Yes, it was the blazing sword "Ragun Raaze," said to be granted by the god of fire to those with burning resolve.
It was exactly the same sword as the one Keen held.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The final battle between the two flame swordsmen began.
While Keen couldn't hide his surprise at an opponent who wielded the same blazing sword, the boy showed a somehow happy smile.

In the middle of the fight, a certain person suddenly came to Keen's mind.
A young boy, seeking strength, holding a crimson sword...

Yes, his true identity was Keen's long-lost younger brother.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Keen had long told himself that he had lost his brother because he had been powerless.
His brother, too, believed he had caused his older brother pain because he himself had lacked strength.

It was precisely because they had lost their beloved family that the two came to seek power.
Yes, so as not to add any more links to the chain of sorrow.

And once again, that feeling had brought the two brothers together.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
One night had passed since the fiery final battle.
Through the battle in which both gave their all, the two flame swords fell into a long slumber.
Perhaps because they had seen the brothers become truly strong,
the swords had taken on a quiet stillness, as if relieved.

With his brother's burning passion engraved in his heart, Keen set off on his journey once more.
To obtain proof of being the strongest next time.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 4: Chapter of Crimson Flames" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r45/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
After that, Keen decided to head for the village of a tribe that had once looked after him.
A few days passed, and as he walked a mountain path in the Safiria Mountains, he suddenly heard music, as if played on beautiful strings, from deep in the thicket beside the path.

Driven by curiosity, Keen pushed into the thicket.
Beyond it was a cliff of bare rock with a small hole in it.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
When Keen peered into the small hole, it was filled with haze inside,
and he couldn't tell what was there, but the music was certainly coming from deep within the hole.

The moment he brought his face closer to get a better look,
everything went black, and Keen lost consciousness.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
When he woke up, Keen was soaking in something like a large pot full of a blue-green liquid.
A fire burned beneath the pot, and the steam of the heated blue-green liquid stung his eyes and nose fiercely.

When Keen hurriedly tried to get out of the pot,
he was pinned down by a creature he'd never seen before.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The creature was about a meter tall and looked human at first glance,
but its face had only a single eyeball and something like a mouth beneath it.
It was naked except for a pelt wrapped around its waist like a grass skirt.

It didn't look very muscular, but it seemed to be quite strong,
for that one creature alone was enough to keep Keen from moving.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
When Keen looked around again, it seemed to be a settlement.
Several dome-shaped structures had a smooth, slick texture unlike anything he had ever seen.

And around the pot Keen was in, dozens of creatures that seemed to be of the same kind as the one pinning him down
were staring at him.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Noticing that Keen had woken up, the one-eyed creatures began making movements like a dance while uttering
words like "Geh-geh" all at once.

His ears began to ring, and just as his consciousness began to fade again, he faintly saw a large shadow approaching from deep in the settlement, shaking the ground.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
With what little consciousness remained, Keen felt himself lifted up, pot and all,
and heard a gulping sound of something being swallowed.

A voice echoed in the head of the unconscious Keen.
"Honerarino　Funarama"

Along with that voice, he heard the music from before once again.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
When he woke up, Keen was in front of the hole he had first peered into.
Looking at it again, the hole was blocked just a few centimeters in.
The music could no longer be heard.
In the front of his shirt was a sheet of parchment written in letters he had never seen.
Then, after staring into space for a while,
Keen returned to his journey.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 5: Chapter of Slumber" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r46/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Having escaped from the basilisk's nest, Keen noticed that it had grown dark.
When he asked a michioshie herb, it told him there was a village called Note nearby.
Keen headed there to find lodging for the night.

After a while, a vast black expanse spread out before him. The sea. Just then,

"Someone! Help me!"

A young woman's scream rang out along with a great splash. Keen ran toward the voice, lit a torch, looked around, and spotted a figure among the waves.
Keen dived into the sea, pulled the woman back to the beach, gathered driftwood from around him, and made a fire.
When Keen patted her cheek, the woman opened her eyes. Her long black hair glowed beautifully in the firelight. Her features were not refined, but she was a beautiful person who brought to mind a startlingly lovely flower. Keen felt his heart flutter.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Her name was Isabella.
She was the daughter of a fisherman in Note Village, and had fallen into the sea while gathering shellfish on the rocks at low tide.
Keen carried Isabella, weak from nearly drowning, on his back to Note Village.

When they reached Isabella's house, her elderly parents came out. Shocked to see Isabella, her mother nursed her and took her to a back room.
Her father said he wanted to thank Keen, so Keen asked to stay the night, and her father gladly agreed, saying that much was nothing.

The next morning, Keen woke to the sense of people outside the house. Looking out the window, he saw young men gathered, each with flowers or food in hand. There was a knock on the door, and Isabella's father came in.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"Are you awake? I hope the bed wasn't too uncomfortable."
"Not at all, thank you. By the way, who are those men?"
"They've come to visit my daughter."

It seemed Isabella's beauty was special even in this village.

"How is your daughter?"
"She seems to be out of danger now. It's thanks to you lighting a fire right away to warm her."

After that, Keen was treated to a breakfast of salt-grilled fish called himiburi. It was a fatty, very delicious fish, but Keen was thinking of Isabella and could hardly taste it.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The next morning, Isabella had fully recovered. She had a kind, cheerful personality, and it was easy to see why the village men were all in love with her.
Keen was one of them, and he lingered on for several days. Having traveled for a long time, Keen was rich in knowledge and experience, and to people who knew only their village, he was a very reliable presence.
Once, he even drove off a troll that appeared on the highway with his skill with the bow, and the villagers came to look at Keen with respect.
Keen felt at home, but reminded himself that he had to search for the Sage's Green Stone, and decided to leave the village. The villagers strongly urged him to stay, but Keen firmly declined and decided to leave the next morning.
That night, a feast was held to send Keen off. As the feast was in full swing, Isabella, who came to pour him a drink, secretly whispered in Keen's ear.

"I'll be waiting at that beach. Please let me thank you properly."

Keen slipped out of the feast, feigning calm, and headed for the beach where he had first met Isabella.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Keen went out onto the beach at night. There was a full moon tonight, and the beach stretching along the bay between the mountains was bathed in moonlight.
Isabella was at the spot where Keen had rescued her. Holding a lamp, she gave a small wave when she saw him.

The two sat on a piece of driftwood and talked about nothing in particular. The night wind off the sea was still a little chilly, and they huddled together.

Just then, a loud noise came from the direction of the village.
Turning around with a start, he saw a giant figure far off at the village meeting hall. A body easily taller than a two-story building: a troll.

Keen ran back to his room and grabbed his bow and arrows. If that troll was showing up in the middle of the village, there was nothing to do but get rid of it. Keen wrote several letters of magic script, tied them to arrows, and headed for the village square.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The troll was tearing the roof off a house. Trolls attack people too, but they are said to have a habit of collecting treasure. It was hard to believe there was any treasure in this fishing village, but it might have sniffed out a few copper coins. The villagers, frightened, were watching from a distance.

Keen looked up at the night sky. The moon was sinking toward the west.
He touched the dagger at his waist, took a deep breath, drew it, and called out to the troll.

"Want treasure? It's over here!"

Keen made the blade sparkle in the moonlight to catch the troll's attention. The troll slowly turned, spotted it, and came toward him with long strides.
Holding the dagger aloft, Keen began luring the troll to the edge of the village.

At the edge of the village, Keen nocked an arrow with a letter attached and loosed it at the troll's leg.
When the arrow hit its shin, the spell in the letter activated, and vines wrapped around the troll's leg.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The vines grew thicker before his eyes, and the troll, its legs caught, fell forward. Keen kept shooting arrows at the troll's hands and jaw, entangling them in vines the same way.
The villagers watching from a distance cheered.

"W-We did it!"
"Not yet! Don't come over here!"

The troll roared as it set about tearing off the vines. With its seemingly endless stamina, it thrashed about, peeling the vines off little by little.
Keen backed away to keep his distance. The troll ripped through the vines and stood up. Keen held up the dagger and lured the troll from the edge of the village to the rocks on the shore.
"I have to buy time until sunrise...!"
Trolls are said to turn to stone when touched by sunlight. Keen meant to hold the troll in place until the morning sun rose and turn it to stone.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The sky had begun to lighten. He had few arrows left.
The troll was sprawled on the rocks of the shore, entangled in thick vines. It was still thrashing with tremendous force, but it also looked a little tired. The troll's eyes found something. Isabella was in its line of sight. The troll was probably hungry. It began thrashing more violently than ever.
"Isabella! Run!"
The moment he shouted, the vines binding the troll burst apart. With unexpected agility, the troll ran toward Isabella. Keen shot an arrow at Isabella's feet. Thick vines enveloped Isabella. He then shot an arrow into the troll's leg, and the giant body tumbled onto the beach. On the sand, the vines' roots didn't hold well. It pulled its leg free at once. But Isabella was covered in vines, and the troll had lost sight of its meal.
"Over here!"
Keen held up his dagger again and lured the troll. Its hunger fueling its rage, the troll lunged furiously to grab Keen. Keen drew it onto the rocks and loosed his last arrow.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 6: Chapter of Love's Path" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r47/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Keen wandered aimlessly alone through an unfamiliar land.
He couldn't hide his surprise at the huge structures lined up and the sheer number of people coming and going.

"Is this some fortress city...? It's a completely different world from where I was."

Thinking this, he recalled what had brought him here.
Was it because of the magic sword he now held...?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The Magic Sword Sekishotuke

Its blade is not very long, but it is a vivid crimson and gives off a dazzling light in the dark.
That light enchants those who see it, letting the wielder control them at will.
Legend says it once instantly stopped the charge of a giant boar made entirely of iron.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Keen was relieved to have the magic sword in his hands.
The journey to find it had been extremely hard. Treacherous roads and powerful monsters.
He had nearly lost his life many times, and he couldn't easily let go of the magic sword he had finally found.
Even in another world, having this magic sword let him stay somewhat calm.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Even so, it wasn't as though the situation would improve.
Just as he was getting used to people staring at him strangely, a man spoke to him.

"Hey, you. You're not from this world, are you?"

He was a well-built man wearing a yellow helmet on his head.
When Keen asked how he knew, the man said,

"Because I'm not from this world either."

The man's name was Eisuka.
By his own account, he had been a fairly skilled sorcerer.
Keen was surprised that there was someone else in the same situation.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
According to Eisuka, there are several unstable spaces in the world,
which sometimes connect to completely different worlds.
The place where the magic sword had been kept was one of them.
When Keen took the magic sword, it must have connected to this world, and he was transported here.

There was something Keen had wanted to ask since meeting Eisuka.
Asking might make all his hardships so far come to nothing,
but he couldn't help asking.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Keen asked. About the thing hanging from Eisuka's waist, exactly the same as the magic sword.
Apparently, the magic sword originally came from this world.

"Here, take a look."

At Eisuka's urging, he looked around.
There were several men holding the same thing as the magic sword.
In this world, the magic sword is nothing rare, and it doesn't display any legendary power.
It only becomes a magic sword when used in the world Keen came from.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
He was a little disappointed that the magic sword was so ordinary, but in his original world it was still a magic sword.
Perhaps sensing this, Eisuka told Keen,

"I'll teach you how to get back to the world we originally came from.
Try this procedure at a certain facility."

The two headed to that facility.
On the way, when Keen asked Eisuka whether he wouldn't return to his original world, Eisuka answered,

"I like this world, you see. I'm not planning to go back for a while yet."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
When they arrived in front of the facility, Keen thanked Eisuka and they parted.

The inside of the facility was divided into several private stalls, each with a water jar.
As he'd been told, Keen entered the stall at the very back and quickly pushed the lever beside the water jar down three times.
Then the water in the jar began to swirl and glow white.
Believing he could return to his original world, Keen leapt into the glowing whirlpool.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 7: Chapter of the Magic Sword" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r48/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Even after parting from Eisuka, Marlo kept walking.
Through unfamiliar towns, over mountains, across rivers, looking up at the sky, toward where the sun rises.
He felt he had been traveling for quite a long time, but when had this journey begun?
He couldn't remember, but Marlo walked on today too.

One day, Marlo came out onto a wasteland where not a single tree or blade of grass grew.
Though he couldn't remember since when he had been traveling, he vaguely recalled
that long, long ago, he had come to a wasteland like this.
When that was, he still couldn't remember.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Back then, Marlo hadn't been traveling alone. There were many people around him.
Living in a big city in a small country, he seemed to have been close to a certain girl.
He and she, who met almost every day, were not lovers.
They were best friends bound by a strong bond; no, comrades in arms.

Yes, Marlo had taken part in a war... apparently.

Apparently, because strangely, he himself couldn't remember it well.
But he and his comrade, that girl, had certainly fought in a wasteland like this.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
They had belonged to a revolutionary army, in other words, rebels against their country. They hadn't fought for peace. Quite the opposite.
This world, so peaceful now, was then in an age of warring states, and every country waged war eagerly to expand its territory. In the middle of such an era, the ruler of their country disliked conflict.
The king, who had lost his parents to war at a young age, was said to have become cowardly from that experience. He thought only of protecting the small country with minimal sacrifice.

Now it was an age peaceful enough to travel alone at leisure, so Marlo still couldn't remember it deeply, but that was apparently how it had been.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"I want to make our country bigger."

The girl said one day.

"It's a tiny country now, but I want to make it big enough that no one can look down on us."

In the eyes of the strong-willed, tomboyish girl, there seemed to dwell a firm resolve.

Her parents, too, had lost their lives in war.
They had been cut down by enemy soldiers who invaded the city, mocked mercilessly as people of a weak nation.

Marlo agreed with her.
It may have been sympathy, but he wanted to make the country bigger and reduce the number of people who suffered sorrow like hers... it seems.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Within the country, they fought against their homeland's ruler. They crossed swords with the king's own soldiers.
The country, weakened as civil war split its forces, became prey to the powerful nations around it and lost more and more territory. Though they knew this, they believed that the only way to move the weak king's heart was to show him the strength of the people's will. The fighting within the country never ceased.

One day, there was a battle in a wasteland.
He noticed that the girl who had been swinging her sword beside him was gone.
Even after the fighting died down, she was nowhere to be seen, and Marlo searched for her.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
She was crouching behind a rock.

"Uuu..."
Worried, he peered into her face, and to his surprise, she was crying.
"What's wrong?!"
Marlo grabbed her slender shoulders, shook her, and asked. Then she said in a tear-soaked voice,
"We were wrong..."

She had been badly wounded in the battle and had hidden behind this rock.
And then, of all people, the king appeared. She tried to raise her sword, but she seemed to have dropped her beloved sword when she left the battlefield, and the scabbard at her waist was empty.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The king neither hurt her nor blamed her, but simply sat quietly beside her and treated her wounds. And he said this:

I don't want to fight a war like this.
The bigger a country becomes, the more matters escape the king's eyes. He can no longer wish for the happiness of all his people. Such a king is no longer a king. I don't want to become such a king.
I only think that if everyone in this small country I hold dear can live with a smile, that's enough.

These words made her realize that she had overlooked what truly mattered. And just as she was about to apologize to the king, behind him were her comrades from the revolutionary army...

Beside the girl shedding tears lay a headless corpse.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Marlo had dragged up this memory from the depths of the depths of his mind, but he realized it didn't seem to be his own. He came from a peaceful country village, and he had never experienced war in his life. He carried a sword for self-defense, just in case, but he preferred magic.

Yet this memory certainly had a vivid sense of presence. There were many odd things about it. The memory of the girl polishing his body, the sensation of being swung around by the girl in a physical sense, the feel of tearing through human skin, and so on...
"...Ah, I see. These are your memories."
Saying so, Marlo gently touched the old sword at his own waist.
The silver one, who resonated with the will of the girl who had owned him, and who still thinks of her.

And so, the one and his blade continue their journey.
Though they can't remember since when they've been traveling, or why.

"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 8: Chapter of Remembrance" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r49/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Since then, Keen had boarded the airship Eye Bird and sat alone by the window of a cabin, gazing outside.
Outside, the sky was clear blue, and a pleasant breeze was blowing.
"Mister."
Turning at the sudden call, he saw a girl in a cute hat and a dress smiling and holding her hand out to Keen.
"Here, this is for you."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r50/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"Hehe, you don't have to be so surprised."
He must have looked quite startled, because the girl laughed at him.
In the girl's hand was a candy.
He didn't like sweets, but there was no need to turn down her kindness.
"Thank you."
When Keen took it, the girl gave a bright smile and left the cabin for the deck.
There was still a little time before they reached their destination.
Keen put the candy in his pocket and decided to go out on deck too.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r50/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
On deck, the passengers were passing the time as they pleased.
Looking around, he saw the girl from before talking cheerfully with an elderly man.
She's not shy at all, he thought as he walked along the deck, when he noticed a young woman clinging to the railing as if she might collapse at any moment.
"Haah......"
"Wh-What's wrong?"
He couldn't help calling out to her.
"No... um... it's embarrassing, but I'm terribly hungry..."
A pitiful sound could be heard.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r50/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"I haven't eaten anything since yesterday...
I thought they'd at least sell food on board, so I jumped on,
but they told me there's nothing like that..."
"I see... but I don't have any food either..."

He remembered that he'd just been given a candy.

"Oh, right, it was a gift, but if a candy will do, please have it."
"R-Really?! Thank you so much...!"

Just then, the girl from before came over.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r50/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
"Miss, this is for you."
Just like before, the girl was smiling and holding out a candy to the woman.
"Huh? Oh, th-thank you..."
When the woman took the candy, the girl gave the same bright smile and walked off.
"Then I'll gratefully accept both of your kindnesses..."
Popping one candy into her mouth with a happy look, the woman asked Keen,
"That girl looked about 10 years old. Do you think she's alone?"
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r50/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
It happened in an instant.
One after another, people burst open, and lizard-like creatures emerged from inside and attacked Keen.
Keen immediately drew his sword and took a stance.
Fortunately, the lizards were not very intelligent and were no match for Keen now.
Before he knew it, the sky had clouded over and grown dim, and the airship was tilting.
Had the pilot turned into a lizard too?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r50/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
He tried to rush to the cockpit, but his body floated into the air and he couldn't kick off the floor.
I'm falling... he thought, and when he looked outside the ship, the girl floating in midair looked his way, smiled,
and transformed into a silver dragon.
Keen lost consciousness.


"The Tale of the Last Sword, Volume 9: Chapter of the Great Sky" End
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r50/c10; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Keen stood at the place called the farthest edge of this world.
Deep in a forest covered with trees so dense the sky couldn't be seen, there was a lake of clear water, with a small shack beside it. The soft morning glow lit them up.
The far side of the lake couldn't be seen, for it was as large as a sea. According to legend, beyond this lake is a waterfall dropping into the abyss, and this place is, as its name says, "the Edge of the World."

Yes, this was a legendary land no one had ever reached. A place everyone thought of as myth or fairy tale.
Keen had kept traveling with this place as his goal, and had finally arrived yesterday.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r51/c3; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Last night, Keen pitched a tent on the lakeshore but didn't sleep in it.
As befitted a remote land without people, the night sky was adorned with countless stars, and seeing them, he lay down
in the grass.
And he looked back on his life until now.

On the days he had wandered the world before setting foot in the land he sought.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r51/c4; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Once, he had taken the life of a brave young elf who lived in the forest.
He remembered that the elf had a girl he loved, but he died without seeing her face.

Once, thinking that what he sought might not be on the ground at all, he had set out into space.
There he became a soldier for the first time, and with no prior experience, Keen struggled, but through hard work he rose all the way to vice admiral.
Life in space had been rather fun too.

He also remembered the strange village at the bottom of a lake, different from this one.
That time, he had nearly been eaten by a bizarre creature like a mushroom house.
That creature's flesh had been truly delicious.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r51/c5; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Once, he had thrown himself into a blazing, truly fiery battle. He had thought the road to the legendary land might open only to the strong.
There he met his owner's long-lost younger brother, and he remembers being deeply moved to find that they shared the same feelings.

Once, drawn in by beautiful music, he had suddenly lost consciousness, and woke up to find himself in a pot over a fire
.
That had been a strange experience. What did the letters on the parchment he found himself holding at that time mean...　There's no way to find out now.

Once, he and a fisherman's daughter living in a fishing village had been drawn to each other. She was a very beautiful girl.
A long time had passed since then; what kind of life had she lived?
Keen hopes she was happy.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r51/c6; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
On this journey, he had even become a magic sword that could control anyone who saw it at will.
He had thought that the land he sought might be another world. But he learned it wasn't, and since he was soon taught a way back to his original world, he appealed to the will of the boy who owned him and returned.

He had been surprised when there was a young man who could sense his feelings like telepathy. Keen had traveled with him for a long time too, for in his usual form, communicating with humans was impossible.
He still sometimes thinks of the girl who was once his master in his memories, but he thinks of that young man just as often.

He also remembered the color of the candy given to him by the girl he met on the airship.
Did the proud dragon do something like that to make humans, who had even rowed out into the sky, learn who the true master of the sky was?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r51/c7; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
...And so Keen gazed at the starry sky, looking back on all that had happened. Thinking it was the last night of this journey, he had meant to stay up all night, but before he knew it he had fallen asleep.
On the last night he could remain in human form, he slept without even dreaming.

Then, feeling the chilly air, he woke early in the morning and gazed at the lake for a while, then took one big deep breath and stood up.
He opened the door of the shack.

Inside the shack were a simple table and chair, and a bed. There was also a cupboard; it looked like one person could live there. But there was no one in sight, and it seemed it hadn't been cleaned in years, for dust danced through the room.
On the table lay a single crumpled sheet of paper, showing its age.

"We, the people of the water, await the sword. May its power bring salvation to the god of the lake."
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r51/c8; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The farthest edge of the world had not always been so.
There had been a small but technologically advanced village. The people who lived peacefully there, grateful for the blessings of the lake and forest, were called "the people of the water."
But that peace was shattered by an invasion by another people. Their village, which had never liked conflict, was soon driven to the brink of destruction. In those final moments, they placed their hopes on a legend handed down in the village since ancient times.
"Long ago, ten holy swords were made in the village. They were scattered across the world, but when the people of the water are in peril, they will come to this land again and give power to the god of the lake."
It is said that a few who managed to escape that battle built a shack deep in the forest, where a barrier kept enemies out, and lived there praying to the swords.

"...I'm sorry I'm so late."
Keen murmured.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0170.json:r51/c9; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Yes, he is a sword.
A holy sword, said to have been forged in this land long ago. He doesn't know what his nine brothers are doing now, but he has returned to his homeland like this. With the power that the smith of the people of the water instilled in him, he traveled sometimes in human form, and sometimes as a sword.
It took a very long time to find his homeland, which had become a legendary land, but he returned safely.
And now, inside this shack, he is about to fall into a long sleep as a sword.
He himself could decide here the incantation that the next one to wake him would have to recite,
and finding a good idea among the memories he had recalled last night, Keen grinned.

"Honerarino　Funarama"

As a hard, metallic voice rang out, dazzling light covered the entire area.
When the light faded, all that remained were a single crumpled sheet of paper and one battered sword.
"The Tale of the Last Sword, Final Volume: Chapter of Silence" End
